files.explanation: An engine-level service: Autoload "SaveGame": reads/writes the saves (JSON in user://saves/). SLOTS save slots (slot_1.json ...); each save keeps, besides the game, a `summary` (where you were - the system, and the planet if you were on one - your ship and credits) for the save / load slot lists. The old single save (user://savegame.json) moves into slot 1. Loading works by putting the saved data in `pending`, then (re)loading the game scene; the game applies `pending` in its _ready(). A save made on a planet carries `landed` ({planet, pos}): the space scene, loading it, goes straight back down there (main.gd), the pilot where you stood (`resume`). (Moved from scripts/save_game.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,462 @@ 
+extends Node
+## Autoload "SaveGame": reads/writes the saves (JSON in user://saves/).
+##
+## SLOTS save slots (slot_1.json ...); each save keeps, besides the game, a
+## `summary` (where you were - the system, and the planet if you were on one -
+## your ship and credits) for the save / load slot lists. The old single save
+## (user://savegame.json) moves into slot 1.
+##
+## Loading works by putting the saved data in `pending`, then (re)loading the
+## game scene; the game applies `pending` in its _ready(). A save made on a
+## planet carries `landed` ({planet, pos}): the space scene, loading it, goes
+## straight back down there (main.gd), the pilot where you stood (`resume`).
+
+const DIR := "user://saves/"
+const SLOTS := 6
+const LEGACY := "user://savegame.json"
+const VERSION := 2
+## Besides the numbered slots: the quicksave (F5 / F9: Keybinds "quicksave",
+## "quickload") and the autosave (every Settings.autosave_minutes - not while
+## you're under attack - and, Settings.autosave_events, on docking, arriving
+## in a system, landing: autosave(why)). Settings > Game chooses.
+const QUICK := 101
+const AUTO := 102
+## Talos opened from a game (F8, or the Esc menu): the game is saved here - a
+## slot of its own, never in the lists - and loaded back when you leave Talos.
+const TALOS := 103
+## A live restart (LiveLink: a change that can't be hot reloaded): the game
+## saved here and loaded back as the game comes up again.
+const LIVE := 104
+const EDITOR_SCENE := "res://scenes/editor/editor.tscn"
+## (the time between periodic autosaves now: Settings.autosave_minutes)
+static func autosave_every() -> float:
+	return float(Settings.autosave_minutes) * 60.0
+const GAME_SCENE := "res://scenes/world/cosmos.tscn"   # (the game: 3D)
+var _auto_t := 300.0
+
+## Save data waiting to be applied by the next game scene that loads.
+var pending: Dictionary = {}
+
+## While you're on a planet surface: the full space game state (as save data)
+## to restore when you take off, and which planet you're on.
+var space_state: Dictionary = {}
+var landed_planet := ""
+## The planet you just took off from (for the take-off animation in space).
+var took_off_from := ""
+## Where the ship was relative to the planet when it landed.
+var orbit_offset := Vector2.ZERO
+## True while switching between space and a planet (keeps the event log).
+var travelling := false
+## Loading a save made on a planet: where the pilot stood ({pos}) - the
+## surface puts you there instead of beside your ship.
+var resume: Dictionary = {}
+## The slot last saved to or loaded from (the slot lists start on it).
+var current_slot := 1
+## True while Talos was opened from a game: leaving Talos goes back to it.
+var talos_return := false
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	_migrate()
+	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS   # (F8 closes Talos over the paused game; autosaves still wait for an unpaused one)
+	# Every save's header read ahead, off the main thread (_head).
+	var paths := []
+	for slot in all_slots():
+		if FileAccess.file_exists(slot_path(slot)):
+			paths.append([slot_path(slot), FileAccess.get_modified_time(slot_path(slot))])
+	_tasks.append(WorkerThreadPool.add_task(func():
+		for pm in paths:
+			_read_head(pm[0], pm[1])))
+
+
+## The worker tasks started here (each waited for: done ones as they're seen, all at exit).
+var _tasks: Array = []
+
+func _reap(all := false) -> void:
+	for t in _tasks.duplicate():
+		if all or WorkerThreadPool.is_task_completed(t):
+			WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion(t)
+			_tasks.erase(t)
+
+
+func _exit_tree() -> void:
+	_reap(true)
+
+
+func slot_path(slot: int) -> String:
+	if slot == QUICK:
+		return DIR + "quick.json"
+	if slot == AUTO:
+		return DIR + "auto.json"
+	if slot == TALOS:
+		return DIR + "talos_resume.json"
+	if slot == LIVE:
+		return DIR + "live_restart.json"
+	return DIR + "slot_%d.json" % slot
+
+
+## Every slot, the quicksave and autosave first.
+func all_slots() -> Array:
+	return [QUICK, AUTO] + range(1, SLOTS + 1)
+
+
+static func slot_name(slot: int) -> String:
+	return {QUICK: "Quicksave", AUTO: "Autosave"}.get(slot, "Slot %d" % slot)
+
+
+## The old single save becomes slot 1.
+func _migrate() -> void:
+	if FileAccess.file_exists(LEGACY) and not FileAccess.file_exists(slot_path(1)):
+		DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(DIR)
+		DirAccess.rename_absolute(LEGACY, slot_path(1))
+
+
+func has_save(slot := -1) -> bool:
+	if slot > 0:
+		return FileAccess.file_exists(slot_path(slot))
+	for i in all_slots():
+		if FileAccess.file_exists(slot_path(i)):
+			return true
+	return false
+
+
+## The slot with the newest save (0: none).
+func latest_slot() -> int:
+	var best := 0
+	var best_t := ""
+	for i in all_slots():
+		var t := saved_at(i)
+		if t != "" and t > best_t:
+			best = i
+			best_t = t
+	return best
+
+
+func save_game(state: Dictionary, slot := -1) -> bool:
+	if slot <= 0:
+		slot = current_slot
+	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(DIR)
+	var data := {
+		"version": VERSION,
+		"saved_at": Time.get_datetime_string_from_system(false, true),
+		"summary": summarize(state),
+		"state": state,
+	}
+	var file := FileAccess.open(slot_path(slot), FileAccess.WRITE)
+	if file == null:
+		push_error("Could not write save: %s" % error_string(FileAccess.get_open_error()))
+		return false
+	file.store_string(JSON.stringify(data, "\t"))
+	if slot <= SLOTS:
+		current_slot = slot
+	return true
+
+
+## Like save_game, written on a worker thread (an autosave: docking,
+## arriving in a system - the JSON of the whole galaxy was ~13 ms of that
+## frame). The state is copied first (the game goes on changing it); the file
+## is written aside and moved into place whole.
+func save_in_background(state: Dictionary, slot: int) -> void:
+	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(DIR)
+	var data := {
+		"version": VERSION,
+		"saved_at": Time.get_datetime_string_from_system(false, true),
+		"summary": summarize(state),
+		"state": state.duplicate(true),
+	}
+	var path := slot_path(slot)
+	_reap()
+	_tasks.append(WorkerThreadPool.add_task(func():
+		var f := FileAccess.open(path + ".part", FileAccess.WRITE)
+		if f == null:
+			return
+		f.store_string(JSON.stringify(data, "\t"))
+		f.close()
+		DirAccess.rename_absolute(path + ".part", path)))
+
+
+## What the slot lists show of a save: {system, planet, ship, credits}.
+static func summarize(state: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	var pl: Dictionary = state.get("player", {})
+	var planet := ""
+	if state.has("landed"):
+		planet = str(Planets.get_planet(str(state["landed"].get("planet", ""))).get("name", ""))
+	var cls := str(pl.get("ship_class", "player"))
+	return {"system": str(Galaxy.system(Galaxy.current_system).get("name", "")), "planet": planet,
+		"ship": str(Shipyard.stats(cls).get("name", "")), "credits": int(pl.get("credits", 0))}
+
+
+## The whole save ({version, saved_at, summary, state}) of a slot (-1: the
+## newest) or {} if missing / corrupt.
+func read_save(slot := -1) -> Dictionary:
+	if slot <= 0:
+		slot = latest_slot()
+	if slot <= 0 or not FileAccess.file_exists(slot_path(slot)):
+		return {}
+	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(FileAccess.get_file_as_string(slot_path(slot)))
+	if parsed is Dictionary and parsed.has("state"):
+		return parsed
+	push_warning("Save file %d is corrupt, ignoring it." % slot)
+	return {}
+
+
+func saved_at(slot := -1) -> String:
+	if slot <= 0:
+		slot = latest_slot()
+	return str(_head(slot).get("saved_at", ""))
+
+
+## A slot's line for the lists: {saved_at, summary} or {} when empty.
+func slot_info(slot: int) -> Dictionary:
+	return _head(slot).duplicate()
+
+
+## A save's header ({saved_at, summary}, {} if none): read once per version of
+## the file (its modified time) and kept - the menus ask for every slot's each
+## time one is built (a scene change); parsing whole saves then was ~20 ms.
+## Read ahead on a worker thread at start-up (_ready).
+var _heads := {}            # path -> [modified time, header]
+var _heads_lock := Mutex.new()
+
+func _head(slot: int) -> Dictionary:
+	var p := slot_path(slot)
+	if slot <= 0 or not FileAccess.file_exists(p):
+		return {}
+	var mt := FileAccess.get_modified_time(p)
+	_heads_lock.lock()
+	var known: Array = _heads.get(p, [])
+	_heads_lock.unlock()
+	if not known.is_empty() and int(known[0]) == mt:
+		return known[1]
+	return _read_head(p, mt)
+
+
+func _read_head(p: String, mt: int) -> Dictionary:
+	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(FileAccess.get_file_as_string(p))
+	var h := {}
+	if parsed is Dictionary and parsed.has("state"):
+		h = {"saved_at": parsed.get("saved_at", ""), "summary": parsed.get("summary", {})}
+	_heads_lock.lock()
+	_heads[p] = [mt, h]
+	_heads_lock.unlock()
+	return h
+
+
+func delete_slot(slot: int) -> void:
+	if FileAccess.file_exists(slot_path(slot)):
+		DirAccess.remove_absolute(slot_path(slot))
+
+
+## Queue a slot's save (-1: the newest) to be applied when the game scene
+## loads. False if there is nothing valid to load.
+func queue_load(slot := -1) -> bool:
+	if slot <= 0:
+		slot = latest_slot()
+	var data := read_save(slot)
+	if data.is_empty():
+		return false
+	pending = data["state"]
+	if slot <= SLOTS:
+		current_slot = slot
+	return true
+
+
+# --- Quicksave, quickload, autosave ---------------------------------------------------------
+
+## The running game, if it can be saved now (`busy_ok`: even paused - docked).
+func _game(busy_ok := false) -> Node:
+	var tree := get_tree()
+	var scene := tree.current_scene if tree else null
+	if scene == null or not scene.has_method("get_save_data") or travelling:
+		return null
+	if scene.has_method("can_save") and not scene.can_save():
+		return null
+	if scene.has_method("build_settled") and not scene.build_settled():
+		return null   # (still being built, a piece a frame: not a game to save yet)
+	if tree.paused and not busy_ok:
+		return null
+	return scene
+
+
+func quicksave() -> bool:
+	var g := _game(true)
+	if g == null:
+		toast("Can't save now")
+		return false
+	if save_game(g.get_save_data(), QUICK):
+		GameLog.post("Quicksaved (F9 to load it).", "good")
+		toast("QUICKSAVED")
+		return true
+	return false
+
+
+func quickload() -> bool:
+	if not has_save(QUICK):
+		toast("No quicksave yet")
+		return false
+	return load_slot(QUICK)
+
+
+## Loads a slot's save (-1: the newest) into the game, under the loading
+## screen (LoadVeil) until it's ready to play - back down on the planet if
+## it was made there. False if there is nothing valid to load.
+func load_slot(slot := -1) -> bool:
+	if get_tree().root.has_node("LoadVeil"):
+		return true   # (already loading)
+	if slot <= 0:
+		slot = latest_slot()
+	if not queue_load(slot):
+		return false
+	travelling = false
+	Cosmos.arrive_from = ""
+	LoadVeil.change_to(GAME_SCENE, {QUICK: "Loading quicksave", AUTO: "Loading autosave", TALOS: "Back to the game", LIVE: "Back to the game - updated"}.get(slot, "Loading slot %d" % slot),
+		func(_progress):
+			CosmosGame.begin_state(pending)
+			pending = {}, "Loading your save")
+	return true
+
+
+## Opens Talos over the running game (F8, or the Esc menu): the game stays
+## as it is underneath - paused, nothing unloaded - and leaving Talos (Back,
+## Esc, F8) puts you straight back in it (close_talos). Talos draws above
+## the game: it and every layer it makes are lifted by TALOS_LAYER. False
+## (and a word on screen) when there's no game to open it over just now.
+const TALOS_LAYER := 400
+var _talos_state := {}
+## The frame Talos over the game closed (the Esc menu under it skips the key
+## that closed it - else that same Esc would close the menu too).
+var talos_closed_frame := -1
+
+func open_talos() -> bool:
+	if talos_overlay() != null:
+		return true
+	var g := _game(true)
+	if g == null:
+		toast("Can't open Talos now")
+		return false
+	var tree := get_tree()
+	_talos_state = {"paused": tree.paused, "galaxy": Galaxy.active, "empire": NeonTheme.empire,
+		"camera": get_viewport().get_camera_2d()}
+	var layer := CanvasLayer.new()
+	layer.name = "TalosOverlay"
+	layer.layer = TALOS_LAYER
+	layer.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS   # (Talos runs; the game under it is paused)
+	if not tree.node_added.is_connected(_lift_layer):
+		tree.node_added.connect(_lift_layer)
+	tree.paused = true
+	talos_return = true
+	var host: Node = TalosNav.scene(EDITOR_SCENE).instantiate()   # (loaded in the background since the game began: TalosNav._warm)
+	host.set("overlay", true)
+	layer.add_child(host)
+	tree.root.add_child(layer)
+	return true
+
+
+## Talos's own layers (its backdrops at -1 / -2, the Library's interface,
+## the guide...) lifted above the game's, in the same order.
+func _lift_layer(n: Node) -> void:
+	var o := talos_overlay()
+	if o != null and n is CanvasLayer and n != o and o.is_ancestor_of(n) and not n.has_meta("talos_lifted"):
+		n.set_meta("talos_lifted", true)
+		# (after its _ready: some set their layer there - the pinned tooltips)
+		(func(): if is_instance_valid(n): n.layer += TALOS_LAYER).call_deferred()
+
+
+## The open Talos (over the game), or null.
+func talos_overlay() -> CanvasLayer:
+	return get_tree().root.get_node_or_null("TalosOverlay") as CanvasLayer
+
+
+## Closes Talos opened over the game: the game as it was - its camera, its
+## look, the galaxy running, paused only if it was. False if none is open.
+func close_talos() -> bool:
+	var o := talos_overlay()
+	if o == null:
+		return false
+	var tree := get_tree()
+	o.name = "TalosClosing"
+	o.queue_free()
+	if tree.node_added.is_connected(_lift_layer):
+		tree.node_added.disconnect(_lift_layer)
+	talos_return = false
+	talos_closed_frame = Engine.get_process_frames()
+	Galaxy.active = bool(_talos_state.get("galaxy", Galaxy.active))
+	NeonTheme.set_empire(str(_talos_state.get("empire", "")))
+	var cam: Camera2D = _talos_state.get("camera") as Camera2D
+	if is_instance_valid(cam) and cam.is_inside_tree():
+		cam.make_current()
+	tree.paused = bool(_talos_state.get("paused", false))
+	_talos_state = {}
+	return true
+
+
+## (Older: Talos opened from a game by saving it first - kept so a save made
+## that way still loads back.)
+func return_from_talos() -> bool:
+	talos_return = false
+	return has_save(TALOS) and load_slot(TALOS)
+
+
+## Saves the game into the autosave (`why` for the log). Not while you're
+## under attack (the scene's in_combat()), nor mid-landing or jump.
+func autosave(why := "") -> bool:
+	if why != "" and not Settings.autosave_events:
+		return false   # (event autosaves switched off)
+	var g := _game(true)
+	if g == null or (g.has_method("in_combat") and g.in_combat()):
+		return false
+	_auto_t = autosave_every()
+	save_in_background(g.get_save_data(), AUTO)
+	GameLog.post("Autosaved%s." % ((" (" + why + ")") if why != "" else ""), "info")
+	return true
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	if Settings.autosave_minutes <= 0:
+		return   # (periodic autosaves off)
+	_auto_t = minf(_auto_t, autosave_every())   # (a shorter interval chosen: applies at once)
+	_auto_t -= delta
+	if _auto_t <= 0.0:
+		_auto_t = 20.0   # (couldn't save now: again in a moment)
+		if _game() != null:
+			autosave()
+
+
+func _unhandled_input(ev: InputEvent) -> void:
+	if Keybinds.pressed(ev, "quicksave") and talos_overlay() == null:
+		if _game(true) != null:
+			quicksave()
+			get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+	elif Keybinds.pressed(ev, "talos"):
+		if talos_overlay() != null:
+			get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+			TalosNav.leave(get_tree())   # (F8 again: back to the game - the tools ask about unsaved edits first)
+		elif _game(true) != null:
+			get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+			open_talos()
+	elif Keybinds.pressed(ev, "quickload") and talos_overlay() == null:   # (not from under Talos)
+		if has_save(QUICK) and get_tree().current_scene and get_tree().current_scene.has_method("get_save_data"):
+			get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+			quickload()
+
+
+## A word on screen for a moment (QUICKSAVED...).
+func toast(text: String) -> void:
+	var layer := CanvasLayer.new()
+	layer.layer = 90
+	var l := Label.new()
+	l.text = text
+	l.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 30)
+	l.add_theme_font_override("font", NeonTheme.heavy_font())
+	l.add_theme_color_override("font_color", NeonTheme.HEAD)
+	l.add_theme_color_override("font_outline_color", Color.BLACK)
+	l.add_theme_constant_override("outline_size", 8)
+	l.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_CENTER_TOP)
+	l.position.y = 120
+	l.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
+	layer.add_child(l)
+	get_tree().root.add_child(layer)
+	var tw := layer.create_tween()
+	tw.tween_interval(0.9)
+	tw.tween_property(l, "modulate:a", 0.0, 0.5)
+	tw.tween_callback(layer.queue_free)

files.explanation: An engine-level service: Autoload "Settings": display, text-size, sound and CRT-filter settings, stored in user://settings.cfg and applied at startup. (Moved from scripts/settings.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,432 @@ 
+extends Node
+## Autoload "Settings": display, text-size, sound and CRT-filter settings,
+## stored in user://settings.cfg and applied at startup.
+
+## Emitted when any text size changes, so open screens can rescale.
+signal text_scale_changed
+
+const PATH := "user://settings.cfg"
+const RESOLUTIONS: Array[Vector2i] = [
+	Vector2i(1152, 648),
+	Vector2i(1280, 720),
+	Vector2i(1366, 768),
+	Vector2i(1600, 900),
+	Vector2i(1920, 1080),
+	Vector2i(2560, 1440),
+	Vector2i(3840, 2160),
+]
+
+const DEFAULT_RESOLUTION := Vector2i(1920, 1080)
+
+## No text smaller than this (px), anywhere - menus, HUD, text drawn on
+## screen - whatever the text size settings: it stays easy to read.
+const MIN_FONT := 12
+## Text size slider range (1.0 = 100%).
+const TEXT_SCALE_MIN := 0.5
+const TEXT_SCALE_MAX := 3.0
+const TEXT_SCALE_STEP := 0.05
+## Kinds of text, each with its own size setting (id -> label in the menu).
+const TEXT_CATEGORIES := {
+	"hud": "HUD",
+	"dialogue": "Story dialogue",
+	"menu": "Menus & panels",
+	"world": "Labels in space",
+}
+
+var resolution := DEFAULT_RESOLUTION
+var fullscreen := false
+var text_scale := {"hud": 1.0, "dialogue": 1.0, "menu": 1.0, "world": 1.0}
+## Volumes, 0 (off) .. 1 (full): everything (the Master bus), the music (the
+## Music bus, see Music), the sound effects (the SFX bus, see Sfx) and the
+## characters' voices (the Voice bus, see Voice).
+const VOLUMES := {"master": "Master", "music": "Music", "sfx": "Sound effects", "voice": "Voices"}
+const VOLUME_DEFAULTS := {"master": 1.0, "music": 0.7, "sfx": 1.0, "voice": 0.8}
+var master_volume := 1.0
+var music_volume := 0.7
+var sfx_volume := 1.0
+var voice_volume := 0.8
+
+## The CRT filter (CrtFilter, shaders/crt.gdshader): off in normal play by
+## default, on during attract mode by default. Every shader parameter can be
+## tuned on its own settings page: [id, label, min, max, step, default,
+## shown x (so 0.38 reads 38), unit, tooltip].
+const CRT_PARAMS := [
+	["curvature", "Curvature", 0.0, 0.2, 0.005, 0.07, 100.0, "", "How much the glass bulges (0 = flat)."],
+	["corner", "Round corners", 0.0, 0.15, 0.005, 0.035, 100.0, "", "How rounded the tube's corners are (0 = square)."],
+	["scanline_px", "Scanline size", 2.0, 8.0, 0.5, 3.0, 1.0, " px", "Screen pixels per scanline."],
+	["scanline_strength", "Scanlines", 0.0, 1.0, 0.01, 0.38, 100.0, "%", "How dark the gaps between the scanlines are."],
+	["mask_strength", "Phosphor mask", 0.0, 0.5, 0.01, 0.14, 100.0, "%", "The red, green and blue stripes of the screen."],
+	["fringe_px", "Colour fringe", 0.0, 4.0, 0.1, 1.2, 1.0, " px", "Red and blue drift apart toward the edges."],
+	["vignette", "Dark rim", 0.0, 1.0, 0.01, 0.32, 100.0, "%", "How much darker the edges of the tube are."],
+	["brightness", "Brightness", 0.6, 1.8, 0.01, 1.2, 100.0, "%", "Overall brightness (makes up for the dark scanlines)."],
+	["flicker", "Flicker", 0.0, 0.06, 0.002, 0.012, 100.0, "%", "A fast shimmer of the picture."],
+	["roll", "Rolling band", 0.0, 0.2, 0.005, 0.04, 100.0, "%", "A faint bright band slowly rolling down the screen."],
+]
+## The FPS counter (FpsCounter): a small frame-rate readout in a corner, with
+## its graph; the settings page has a switch for it. On by default while the
+## game is run from the project (development), off in exported builds (the
+## versions players get: itch.io, the downloads).
+static func fps_counter_default() -> bool:
+	return not OS.has_feature("template")
+var fps_counter := fps_counter_default()
+
+## Autosaves (SaveGame.autosave): every this many minutes (0: never), and
+## (autosave_events) on docking, arriving in a system and landing.
+const AUTOSAVE_CHOICES := [0, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30]
+const AUTOSAVE_DEFAULT := 5
+var autosave_minutes := AUTOSAVE_DEFAULT
+var autosave_events := true
+
+func set_fps_counter(on: bool) -> void:
+	fps_counter = on
+	_queue_save()
+
+
+## How the characters on foot are drawn: "3d" - the automaton's actual 3D model,
+## live (Stage3D; the pirates from the sprites rendered from theirs); "sprites" -
+## the animations rendered from the models, for all; "classic" - the hand-drawn
+## two-pose sheets (the backup). Characters made after the change follow it (the
+## next landing).
+const CHARACTER_GRAPHICS := [["3d", "3D model"], ["sprites", "Rendered sprites"], ["classic", "Classic sprites"]]
+var character_graphics := "3d"
+
+func set_character_graphics(mode: String) -> void:
+	character_graphics = mode if CHARACTER_GRAPHICS.any(func(m): return m[0] == mode) else "3d"
+	_apply_character_graphics()
+	_queue_save()
+
+
+func _apply_character_graphics() -> void:
+	pass   # (the 2D game's character graphics: gone - the 3D game draws its models)
+
+
+## Anti-aliasing (the 3D game's view: edges, the stars, thin plants): its
+## modes, from none to the smoothest. MSAA smooths geometry's edges, FXAA
+## blurs jagged edges cheaply after the picture's drawn, TAA (temporal) also
+## steadies what shimmers from frame to frame (stars, grass) at a little blur.
+const ANTIALIAS := [["off", "Off"], ["fxaa", "FXAA (fastest)"], ["msaa2", "MSAA 2x"], ["msaa4", "MSAA 4x"],
+	["msaa8", "MSAA 8x"], ["taa", "TAA + MSAA 2x (steadiest)"]]
+var antialias := "msaa2"
+
+func set_antialias(mode: String) -> void:
+	antialias = mode if ANTIALIAS.any(func(m): return m[0] == mode) else "msaa2"
+	apply_antialias()
+	_queue_save()
+
+
+func apply_antialias() -> void:
+	var vp := get_tree().root if is_inside_tree() else null
+	if vp == null:
+		return
+	vp.msaa_3d = {"msaa2": Viewport.MSAA_2X, "msaa4": Viewport.MSAA_4X, "msaa8": Viewport.MSAA_8X, "taa": Viewport.MSAA_2X}.get(antialias, Viewport.MSAA_DISABLED)
+	vp.screen_space_aa = Viewport.SCREEN_SPACE_AA_FXAA if antialias == "fxaa" else Viewport.SCREEN_SPACE_AA_DISABLED   # (FXAA on top of MSAA only blurred, at its own cost)
+	vp.use_taa = antialias == "taa"
+
+
+## The planets' ground as 3D geometry (Ground3D) - off: the 2D tiles drawn as
+## pictures (the fallback). From the next landing.
+var terrain_3d := true
+
+func set_terrain_3d(on: bool) -> void:
+	terrain_3d = on
+	_queue_save()
+
+
+const CRT_ON_DEFAULT := false
+const CRT_ATTRACT_DEFAULT := true
+var crt_on := CRT_ON_DEFAULT                # always on
+var crt_attract := CRT_ATTRACT_DEFAULT      # on during attract mode
+var crt_preview := false                    # (the CRT settings page is open)
+var crt := {}                               # id -> value
+
+
+static func crt_default(id: String) -> float:
+	for p in CRT_PARAMS:
+		if p[0] == id:
+			return p[5]
+	return 0.0
+
+
+func set_crt(id: String, value: float) -> void:
+	for p in CRT_PARAMS:
+		if p[0] == id:
+			crt[id] = clampf(value, p[2], p[3])
+	_queue_save()
+
+
+func set_crt_switch(attract: bool, on: bool) -> void:
+	if attract:
+		crt_attract = on
+	else:
+		crt_on = on
+	_queue_save()
+
+
+## The CRT filter's parameters (not the switches) back to their defaults.
+func reset_crt() -> void:
+	for p in CRT_PARAMS:
+		crt[p[0]] = p[5]
+	_queue_save()
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	if bot_arg() and DisplayServer.get_name() != "headless":
+		DisplayServer.window_set_flag(DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_NO_FOCUS, true)
+	reset_crt()
+	load_settings()
+	apply()
+	apply_volumes()
+	# The neon GUI look (see NeonTheme), merged into Godot's default theme:
+	# every Control falls back to it - including those under CanvasLayers
+	# (HUD, panels) and popup windows (menus, dropdowns, tooltips), which a
+	# theme set on the root window doesn't reach.
+	ThemeDB.get_default_theme().merge_with(NeonTheme.build())
+	get_tree().node_added.connect(_on_node_added)
+	get_tree().root.add_child.call_deferred(CrtFilter.new())
+	get_tree().root.add_child.call_deferred(FpsCounter.new())
+
+
+# --- Text sizes ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## Text added after its screen was built - a page rebuilt after a change, a
+## row added to a list - gets that screen's text size (UI.fit_text: the
+## screens UI.scale_fonts scaled are marked) and never less than MIN_FONT.
+## Gathered as they come, fitted once at the end of the frame (before it's drawn).
+var _text_added: Array[Control] = []
+
+func _on_node_added(n: Node) -> void:
+	if not n is Control:
+		return   # (most nodes added in play - shots, sparks, creatures - aren't: one check)
+	if n is Label or n is Button or n is RichTextLabel or n is LineEdit or n is TextEdit or n is ItemList or n is Tree:
+		if _text_added.is_empty():
+			_fit_added_text.call_deferred()
+		_text_added.append(n)
+
+
+func _fit_added_text() -> void:
+	var list := _text_added
+	_text_added = []
+	for n in list:
+		if is_instance_valid(n) and n.is_inside_tree():
+			UI.fit_text(n)
+
+
+func font_scale(category: String) -> float:
+	return text_scale.get(category, 1.0)
+
+
+## A font size for `category`, scaled from the size it was designed at.
+func fs(category: String, base_size: int) -> int:
+	return maxi(MIN_FONT, roundi(base_size * font_scale(category)))
+
+
+func set_text_scale(category: String, value: float) -> void:
+	value = clampf(value, TEXT_SCALE_MIN, TEXT_SCALE_MAX)
+	if is_equal_approx(text_scale.get(category, 1.0), value):
+		return
+	text_scale[category] = value
+	text_scale_changed.emit()
+	_queue_save()
+
+
+func volume(kind: String) -> float:
+	return get(kind + "_volume")
+
+
+## Sets a volume ("master", "music" or "sfx", 0..1) and applies it at once.
+func set_volume(kind: String, value: float) -> void:
+	set(kind + "_volume", clampf(value, 0.0, 1.0))
+	apply_volumes()
+	_queue_save()
+
+
+func set_sfx_volume(value: float) -> void:
+	set_volume("sfx", value)
+
+
+func apply_volumes() -> void:
+	var m := AudioServer.get_bus_index("Master")
+	# (--mute among the user args: playtests run silent - the saved volumes untouched)
+	AudioServer.set_bus_mute(m, master_volume <= 0.001 or muted_arg())
+	AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(m, linear_to_db(maxf(master_volume, 0.001)))
+	for n in ["/root/Sfx", "/root/Music", "/root/Voice"]:
+		var node := get_node_or_null(n)
+		if node:
+			node.apply_volume()
+
+
+## Sliders change values many times a second; write the file once they settle.
+var _save_queued := false
+
+func _queue_save() -> void:
+	if not is_inside_tree():  # too early for timers: just save now
+		save_settings()
+		return
+	if _save_queued:
+		return
+	_save_queued = true
+	await get_tree().create_timer(0.5, true).timeout
+	_save_queued = false
+	save_settings()
+
+
+## Everything back to its default: resolution, fullscreen, text sizes,
+## volumes and the CRT filter.
+func reset_to_defaults() -> void:
+	resolution = DEFAULT_RESOLUTION
+	fullscreen = false
+	for category in text_scale:
+		text_scale[category] = 1.0
+	for k in VOLUME_DEFAULTS:
+		set(k + "_volume", VOLUME_DEFAULTS[k])
+	crt_on = CRT_ON_DEFAULT
+	crt_attract = CRT_ATTRACT_DEFAULT
+	fps_counter = fps_counter_default()
+	character_graphics = "3d"
+	_apply_character_graphics()
+	antialias = "msaa2"
+	apply_antialias()
+	terrain_3d = true
+	autosave_minutes = AUTOSAVE_DEFAULT
+	autosave_events = true
+	reset_crt()
+	apply_volumes()
+	apply()
+	save_settings()
+	text_scale_changed.emit()
+
+
+func _exit_tree() -> void:
+	if _save_queued:  # quitting right after moving a slider
+		save_settings()
+	Icons.wait_all()   # (painting tasks still running at exit: waited for)
+
+
+# --- Display ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## Resolutions that fit on the current screen.
+func available_resolutions() -> Array[Vector2i]:
+	var screen := DisplayServer.screen_get_size()
+	var result: Array[Vector2i] = []
+	for r in RESOLUTIONS:
+		if r.x <= screen.x and r.y <= screen.y:
+			result.append(r)
+	if result.is_empty():
+		result.append(RESOLUTIONS[0])
+	return result
+
+
+## A web build (itch.io and the like): the browser owns the window - no
+## sizes to pick, no window to move, fullscreen only from a click.
+static func on_web() -> bool:
+	return OS.has_feature("web")
+
+
+## A phone or a tablet (the web build on one, or a mobile export).
+static func on_phone() -> bool:
+	return OS.has_feature("web_android") or OS.has_feature("web_ios") or OS.has_feature("mobile")
+
+
+func apply() -> void:
+	if on_web():
+		if fullscreen:
+			DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN)
+		return
+	if fullscreen:
+		DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN)
+	else:
+		DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED)
+		# Resize after the mode change has taken effect.
+		_resize_window.call_deferred()
+
+
+func _resize_window() -> void:
+	# Don't open a window bigger than the screen (e.g. 1920x1080 on a laptop).
+	var fits := available_resolutions()
+	var size := resolution if resolution in fits else fits[-1]
+	DisplayServer.window_set_size(size)
+	var screen := DisplayServer.window_get_current_screen()
+	var origin := DisplayServer.screen_get_position(screen)
+	var screen_size := DisplayServer.screen_get_size(screen)
+	var at := window_at_arg()
+	DisplayServer.window_set_position(at if at != Vector2i(-1, -1) else origin + (screen_size - size) / 2)
+
+
+## `-- --window-at=X,Y` on the command line (playtests): the window goes there
+## instead of the screen's centre. (-1, -1) if not given.
+## The user arg --mute: the master volume at zero for this run (playtests).
+static func muted_arg() -> bool:
+	return "--mute" in OS.get_cmdline_user_args()
+
+
+## The user arg --bot: a window opened by Claude's tools (tests, tours, shots):
+## it never takes the keyboard focus, and the 3D game doesn't capture the
+## mouse in it - the user works on undisturbed.
+static func bot_arg() -> bool:
+	return "--bot" in OS.get_cmdline_user_args()
+
+
+static func window_at_arg() -> Vector2i:
+	for a in OS.get_cmdline_user_args():
+		if a.begins_with("--window-at="):
+			var xy := a.trim_prefix("--window-at=").split(",")
+			if xy.size() == 2:
+				return Vector2i(int(xy[0]), int(xy[1]))
+	return Vector2i(-1, -1)
+
+
+# --- Saving ----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func save_settings() -> void:
+	var cfg := ConfigFile.new()
+	cfg.set_value("display", "resolution", resolution)
+	cfg.set_value("display", "fullscreen", fullscreen)
+	for category in text_scale:
+		cfg.set_value("text", category, text_scale[category])
+	for k in VOLUMES:
+		cfg.set_value("audio", k, volume(k))
+	cfg.set_value("display", "fps_counter", fps_counter)
+	cfg.set_value("display", "character_graphics", character_graphics)
+	cfg.set_value("display", "terrain_3d", terrain_3d)
+	cfg.set_value("display", "antialias", antialias)
+	cfg.set_value("game", "autosave_minutes", autosave_minutes)
+	cfg.set_value("game", "autosave_events", autosave_events)
+	cfg.set_value("crt", "on", crt_on)
+	cfg.set_value("crt", "attract", crt_attract)
+	for k in crt:
+		cfg.set_value("crt", k, crt[k])
+	cfg.save(PATH)
+
+
+## The first run on a phone: the text a size up (a 1080-line screen a few inches across).
+const PHONE_TEXT := {"hud": 1.3, "dialogue": 1.3, "menu": 1.25, "world": 1.2}
+
+func load_settings() -> void:
+	var cfg := ConfigFile.new()
+	if cfg.load(PATH) != OK:
+		if on_phone():
+			text_scale.merge(PHONE_TEXT, true)
+		return
+	resolution = cfg.get_value("display", "resolution", resolution)
+	fullscreen = cfg.get_value("display", "fullscreen", fullscreen)
+	for category in text_scale:
+		text_scale[category] = clampf(float(cfg.get_value("text", category, 1.0)), TEXT_SCALE_MIN, TEXT_SCALE_MAX)
+	for k in VOLUMES:
+		set(k + "_volume", clampf(float(cfg.get_value("audio", k, VOLUME_DEFAULTS[k])), 0.0, 1.0))
+	fps_counter = bool(cfg.get_value("display", "fps_counter", fps_counter_default()))
+	character_graphics = str(cfg.get_value("display", "character_graphics", "3d"))
+	if not CHARACTER_GRAPHICS.any(func(m): return m[0] == character_graphics):
+		character_graphics = "3d"
+	_apply_character_graphics()
+	terrain_3d = bool(cfg.get_value("display", "terrain_3d", true))
+	antialias = str(cfg.get_value("display", "antialias", "msaa2"))
+	apply_antialias.call_deferred()
+	pass
+	autosave_minutes = int(cfg.get_value("game", "autosave_minutes", AUTOSAVE_DEFAULT))
+	if not autosave_minutes in AUTOSAVE_CHOICES:
+		autosave_minutes = AUTOSAVE_DEFAULT
+	autosave_events = bool(cfg.get_value("game", "autosave_events", true))
+	crt_on = bool(cfg.get_value("crt", "on", CRT_ON_DEFAULT))
+	crt_attract = bool(cfg.get_value("crt", "attract", CRT_ATTRACT_DEFAULT))
+	for p in CRT_PARAMS:
+		crt[p[0]] = clampf(float(cfg.get_value("crt", p[0], p[5])), p[2], p[3])

files.explanation: An engine-level service: Autoload "Sfx": sound effects. Sounds live in res://sounds/<group>/ as takes <name>_1.ogg, <name>_2.ogg ... (tools/sfx_pirate.py makes the pirate's); a sound is called by "<group>/<name>" and each time one of its takes plays, at a slightly random pitch, so repeats don't sound the same. Sfx.play_at("pirate/shot", where, parent) # in the world: fades with distance from the camera Sfx.play("pirate/loot_take") # flat (for you: picking things up, the UI) Sfx.play_world("space/boom_big", global_pos) # at a global point, in the FX layer / scene var hum := Sfx.loop_at("space/station_hum", station) # a looping sound on a node (yours to stop) Everything goes through the "SFX" bus, whose volume is Settings.sfx_volume. A sound can't stack up endlessly: at most MAX_EACH of one sound play at once (a band of pirates firing), MAX_ALL in all. (Moved from scripts/sfx.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,198 @@ 
+extends Node
+## Autoload "Sfx": sound effects. Sounds live in res://sounds/<group>/ as
+## takes <name>_1.ogg, <name>_2.ogg ... (tools/sfx_pirate.py makes the
+## pirate's); a sound is called by "<group>/<name>" and each time one of its
+## takes plays, at a slightly random pitch, so repeats don't sound the same.
+##
+##   Sfx.play_at("pirate/shot", where, parent)   # in the world: fades with distance from the camera
+##   Sfx.play("pirate/loot_take")                # flat (for you: picking things up, the UI)
+##   Sfx.play_world("space/boom_big", global_pos) # at a global point, in the FX layer / scene
+##   var hum := Sfx.loop_at("space/station_hum", station)   # a looping sound on a node (yours to stop)
+##
+## Everything goes through the "SFX" bus, whose volume is Settings.sfx_volume.
+## A sound can't stack up endlessly: at most MAX_EACH of one sound play at
+## once (a band of pirates firing), MAX_ALL in all.
+
+const DIR := "res://sounds/"
+const BUS := "SFX"
+const MAX_EACH := 6
+const MAX_ALL := 40
+const MAX_TAKES := 12
+## How far a sound in the world carries (px), and how fast it fades.
+const RANGE := 1500.0
+const FALLOFF := 1.6
+
+var _takes := {}                    # "group/name" -> [AudioStream, ...]
+var _playing := {}                  # "group/name" -> [players]
+var _count := 0
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	if AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS) < 0:
+		AudioServer.add_bus()
+		var i := AudioServer.bus_count - 1
+		AudioServer.set_bus_name(i, BUS)
+		AudioServer.set_bus_send(i, "Master")
+	apply_volume()
+	set_process(false)
+
+
+var _warm_queue: Array = []         # sounds still to load ahead (warm)
+
+
+## Loads every sound in `folder` ("space") ahead - one a frame, in the
+## background: the first explosion of a fight doesn't also read its sound
+## from disk (a few ms in that frame).
+## (once a run per folder: listing it was ~5 ms of each space scene's first
+## frame; every take requested from a background loader - _process collects
+## them as they're done, takes() takes one ready-made)
+static var _listed := {}
+func warm(folder: String) -> void:
+	if _listed.has(folder):
+		return
+	_listed[folder] = true
+	for f in ResourceLoader.list_directory(DIR + folder):
+		if f.get_extension() != "ogg":
+			continue
+		var key := folder + "/" + f.get_basename().rsplit("_", true, 1)[0]
+		if not _takes.has(key) and not _warm_queue.has(key):
+			_warm_queue.append(key)
+			_request_queue.append(key)
+	set_process(not _warm_queue.is_empty())
+
+
+var _request_queue: Array = []   # keys whose takes are still to be asked for (a few a frame)
+
+func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
+	for i in 3:
+		if _request_queue.is_empty():
+			break
+		var rk: String = _request_queue.pop_front()
+		for k in range(1, MAX_TAKES + 1):
+			var path := "%s%s_%d.ogg" % [DIR, rk, k]
+			if not ResourceLoader.exists(path):
+				break
+			if ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get_status(path) == ResourceLoader.THREAD_LOAD_INVALID_RESOURCE:
+				ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request(path)
+	if _warm_queue.is_empty():
+		set_process(false)
+		return
+	var key: String = _warm_queue[0]
+	if _takes.has(key):
+		_warm_queue.pop_front()
+		return
+	var path := "%s%s_1.ogg" % [DIR, key]
+	if ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get_status(path) == ResourceLoader.THREAD_LOAD_IN_PROGRESS:
+		return   # (still loading: next frame)
+	takes(_warm_queue.pop_front())
+
+
+## The SFX bus at Settings.sfx_volume (0 = silent, 1 = full).
+func apply_volume() -> void:
+	var i := AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS)
+	if i < 0:
+		return
+	var v: float = Settings.sfx_volume
+	AudioServer.set_bus_mute(i, v <= 0.001)
+	AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(i, linear_to_db(maxf(v, 0.001)))
+
+
+## Every take of a sound (loaded once).
+func takes(key: String) -> Array:
+	if not _takes.has(key):
+		var found := []
+		for k in range(1, MAX_TAKES + 1):
+			var path := "%s%s_%d.ogg" % [DIR, key, k]
+			if not ResourceLoader.exists(path):
+				break
+			var bg := ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get_status(path) != ResourceLoader.THREAD_LOAD_INVALID_RESOURCE
+			found.append(ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get(path) if bg else load(path))
+		_takes[key] = found
+	return _takes[key]
+
+
+func _free_slot(key: String) -> bool:
+	var live: Array = _playing.get(key, []).filter(func(p): return is_instance_valid(p))
+	_playing[key] = live
+	return live.size() < MAX_EACH and _count < MAX_ALL
+
+
+func _track(key: String, p: Node) -> void:
+	_playing[key].append(p)
+	_count += 1
+	p.tree_exited.connect(func(): _count -= 1)
+
+
+## Plays a sound in the world at `at` (in `parent`'s coordinates): it fades
+## with distance from the camera. volume_db shifts it (quieter footsteps);
+## pitch: how much the pitch may wander (0.06 = +-6 %). Null if it didn't play.
+func play_at(key: String, at: Vector2, parent: Node, volume_db := 0.0, pitch := 0.06) -> AudioStreamPlayer2D:
+	var list := takes(key)
+	if list.is_empty() or parent == null or not parent.is_inside_tree() or not _free_slot(key):
+		return null
+	var p := AudioStreamPlayer2D.new()
+	p.stream = list.pick_random()
+	p.position = at
+	p.bus = BUS
+	p.volume_db = volume_db
+	p.pitch_scale = 1.0 + randf_range(-pitch, pitch)
+	p.max_distance = RANGE
+	p.attenuation = FALLOFF
+	p.finished.connect(p.queue_free)
+	parent.add_child(p)
+	_track(key, p)
+	p.play()
+	return p
+
+
+## Plays a sound at a global position: in the FX layer (group "fx_layer") or
+## else the current scene.
+func play_world(key: String, global_at: Vector2, volume_db := 0.0, pitch := 0.06) -> AudioStreamPlayer2D:
+	var tree := get_tree()
+	var layer: Node = tree.get_first_node_in_group("fx_layer")
+	if layer == null:
+		layer = tree.current_scene
+	if not layer is Node2D:
+		return null
+	return play_at(key, (layer as Node2D).to_local(global_at), layer, volume_db, pitch)
+
+
+## A looping sound on `node` (its first take, looping), playing: it moves with
+## the node and goes when it does. Not counted against the caps; the caller
+## turns it up / down / stops it. Null if the sound doesn't exist.
+func loop_at(key: String, node: Node, volume_db := 0.0, max_distance := RANGE) -> AudioStreamPlayer2D:
+	var list := takes(key)
+	if list.is_empty() or node == null:
+		return null
+	var st: AudioStream = list[0]
+	if st is AudioStreamOggVorbis:
+		st.loop = true
+	var p := AudioStreamPlayer2D.new()
+	p.stream = st
+	p.bus = BUS
+	p.volume_db = volume_db
+	p.max_distance = max_distance
+	p.attenuation = FALLOFF
+	node.add_child(p)
+	if p.is_inside_tree():
+		p.play()
+	else:
+		p.ready.connect(p.play)
+	return p
+
+
+## Plays a sound flat - not in the world (yours: loot you pick up, the UI).
+func play(key: String, volume_db := 0.0, pitch := 0.04) -> AudioStreamPlayer:
+	var list := takes(key)
+	if list.is_empty() or not _free_slot(key):
+		return null
+	var p := AudioStreamPlayer.new()
+	p.stream = list.pick_random()
+	p.bus = BUS
+	p.volume_db = volume_db
+	p.pitch_scale = 1.0 + randf_range(-pitch, pitch)
+	p.finished.connect(p.queue_free)
+	add_child(p)
+	_track(key, p)
+	p.play()
+	return p

files.explanation: An engine-level service: A shader-drawn backdrop (a planet, a nebula) drawn into a picture a few times a second instead of every frame: their noise shaders (several 3D noise fields a pixel) were half of a space frame's GPU time, and what they show - a slow turn, a slow drift - doesn't need 600 pictures a second. The source (a ColorRect with its ShaderMaterial) is moved (a frame or a few later: _build, one a frame) into an off-screen viewport (at most max_px across); a TextureRect shows that viewport's picture where the source was, drawn with the source's blend (premultiplied for planets, additive for nebulae). The picture is renewed `hz` times a second while it's on screen; off screen not at all. holder.add_child(ShaderCache.wrap(rect, 12.0)) (rect: positioned and sized already) (Moved from scripts/shader_cache.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,96 @@ 
+class_name ShaderCache
+extends Control
+## A shader-drawn backdrop (a planet, a nebula) drawn into a picture a few
+## times a second instead of every frame: their noise shaders (several 3D
+## noise fields a pixel) were half of a space frame's GPU time, and what they
+## show - a slow turn, a slow drift - doesn't need 600 pictures a second.
+## The source (a ColorRect with its ShaderMaterial) is moved (a frame or a few
+## later: _build, one a frame) into an off-screen viewport (at most max_px across); a TextureRect shows that
+## viewport's picture where the source was, drawn with the source's blend
+## (premultiplied for planets, additive for nebulae). The picture is renewed
+## `hz` times a second while it's on screen; off screen not at all.
+##   holder.add_child(ShaderCache.wrap(rect, 12.0))      (rect: positioned and sized already)
+
+var hz := 10.0
+var _vp: SubViewport
+var _t := 0.0
+var _src: Control
+var _max_px := 1024.0
+var _blend := CanvasItemMaterial.BLEND_MODE_PREMULT_ALPHA
+## One cache is set up a frame (a viewport each: ~6 ms; a system's planets and
+## nebulae all at once were 70 ms of its first frame) - till then the source
+## draws itself, live.
+static var _turn := -1
+
+
+static func wrap(src: Control, hz_ := 10.0, max_px := 1024.0, blend := CanvasItemMaterial.BLEND_MODE_PREMULT_ALPHA) -> ShaderCache:
+	var c := ShaderCache.new()
+	c.hz = hz_
+	c.name = "ShaderCache"
+	c.position = src.position
+	c.size = src.size
+	c.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	# (Like the shader it stands for, it runs whatever the game does - paused,
+	# or a scene still being built a piece a frame: its picture is ready by
+	# the time the scene shows.)
+	c.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	c._src = src
+	c._max_px = max_px
+	c._blend = blend
+	src.position = Vector2.ZERO
+	c.add_child(src)
+	return c
+
+
+## Moves the source into its viewport and shows the viewport's picture in its place.
+func _build() -> void:
+	var src := _src
+	var k := minf(1.0, _max_px / maxf(maxf(src.size.x, src.size.y), 1.0))
+	_vp = SubViewport.new()
+	_vp.transparent_bg = true
+	_vp.disable_3d = true
+	_vp.size = Vector2i(maxi(1, ceili(src.size.x * k)), maxi(1, ceili(src.size.y * k)))
+	_vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE
+	remove_child(src)
+	src.scale = Vector2(k, k)
+	_vp.add_child(src)
+	add_child(_vp)
+	var view := TextureRect.new()
+	view.name = "Picture"
+	view.texture = _vp.get_texture()
+	view.expand_mode = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
+	view.stretch_mode = TextureRect.STRETCH_SCALE
+	view.size = size
+	view.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	var m := CanvasItemMaterial.new()
+	m.blend_mode = _blend
+	view.material = m
+	add_child(view)
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	if _vp == null:
+		if not is_instance_valid(_src):
+			return   # (its scene being taken apart, the leaves first)
+		var f := Engine.get_process_frames()
+		if f != _turn:
+			_turn = f
+			_build()
+		return
+	if not is_instance_valid(_vp):
+		return
+	_t -= delta
+	if _t > 0.0:
+		return
+	if not _on_screen():
+		_t = 0.2   # (looked at again soon: it may come into view)
+		return
+	_t = 1.0 / hz
+	_vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE
+
+
+func _on_screen() -> bool:
+	if not is_visible_in_tree():
+		return false
+	var r := get_global_transform_with_canvas() * Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size)
+	return get_viewport_rect().grow(64.0).intersects(r)

files.explanation: An engine-level service: Many images packed into one texture, so what's drawn from them batches: Godot draws consecutive sprites / tiles of the same texture in one draw call, and every change of texture starts another - a planet's ground and buildings, a texture per piece, were ~1000 draw calls a frame. var a := TextureAtlas.pack(images) -> [Image, [Vector2i top-left or null per image]] Each image gets PAD px of its own edge pixels round it (so filtering at its edge never fades to clear or bleeds a neighbour in), packed in rows WIDTH wide. (Moved from scripts/texture_atlas.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,94 @@ 
+class_name TextureAtlas
+## Many images packed into one texture, so what's drawn from them batches:
+## Godot draws consecutive sprites / tiles of the same texture in one draw
+## call, and every change of texture starts another - a planet's ground and
+## buildings, a texture per piece, were ~1000 draw calls a frame.
+##   var a := TextureAtlas.pack(images)   -> [Image, [Vector2i top-left or null per image]]
+## Each image gets PAD px of its own edge pixels round it (so filtering at its
+## edge never fades to clear or bleeds a neighbour in), packed in rows WIDTH wide.
+
+const PAD := 3
+const WIDTH := 4096
+
+
+static func pack(images: Array, width := WIDTH) -> Array:
+	var pos := []
+	var imgs := []
+	var x := PAD
+	var y := PAD
+	var row_h := 0
+	for img0 in images:
+		var img: Image = img0
+		if img == null or img.is_empty():
+			pos.append(null)
+			imgs.append(null)
+			continue
+		if img.is_compressed():
+			img = img.duplicate()
+			img.decompress()
+		if img.has_mipmaps():
+			img = img.duplicate()
+			img.clear_mipmaps()
+		if img.get_format() != Image.FORMAT_RGBA8:
+			img = img.duplicate()
+			img.convert(Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
+		if x + img.get_width() + PAD > width:
+			x = PAD
+			y += row_h + 2 * PAD
+			row_h = 0
+		pos.append(Vector2i(x, y))
+		imgs.append(img)
+		x += img.get_width() + 2 * PAD   # (each image's own PAD of edge pixels on either side)
+		row_h = maxi(row_h, img.get_height())
+	if imgs.all(func(im): return im == null):
+		return [null, pos]
+	var atlas := Image.create_empty(width, y + row_h + PAD, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
+	for i in imgs.size():
+		if imgs[i] == null:
+			continue
+		var im: Image = imgs[i]
+		var p: Vector2i = pos[i]
+		var w := im.get_width()
+		var h := im.get_height()
+		atlas.blit_rect(im, Rect2i(Vector2i.ZERO, im.get_size()), p)
+		for k in range(1, PAD + 1):
+			atlas.blit_rect(im, Rect2i(0, 0, w, 1), p + Vector2i(0, -k))
+			atlas.blit_rect(im, Rect2i(0, h - 1, w, 1), p + Vector2i(0, h - 1 + k))
+		for k in range(1, PAD + 1):
+			atlas.blit_rect(atlas, Rect2i(p.x, p.y - PAD, 1, h + 2 * PAD), Vector2i(p.x - k, p.y - PAD))
+			atlas.blit_rect(atlas, Rect2i(p.x + w - 1, p.y - PAD, 1, h + 2 * PAD), Vector2i(p.x + w - 1 + k, p.y - PAD))
+	return [atlas, pos]
+
+
+## AtlasTextures for `images` (null where an image was missing), all regions
+## of one texture.
+static func textures(images: Array, width := WIDTH) -> Array:
+	var packed := pack(images, width)
+	var out := []
+	if packed[0] == null:
+		out.resize(images.size())
+		return out
+	var tex := ImageTexture.create_from_image(packed[0])
+	for i in images.size():
+		if packed[1][i] == null:
+			out.append(null)
+			continue
+		var at := AtlasTexture.new()
+		at.atlas = tex
+		at.region = Rect2(packed[1][i], (images[i] as Image).get_size())
+		out.append(at)
+	return out
+
+
+## A TileSetAtlasSource showing `tex` - an AtlasTexture as a region of its
+## atlas (no padded copy of its own: Godot's texture padding would make each
+## source a texture again, unbatchable).
+static func set_source_texture(src: TileSetAtlasSource, tex: Texture2D) -> void:
+	if tex is AtlasTexture and (tex as AtlasTexture).atlas != null:
+		src.texture = (tex as AtlasTexture).atlas
+		src.margins = Vector2i((tex as AtlasTexture).region.position)
+		src.use_texture_padding = false
+	else:
+		src.texture = tex
+		src.margins = Vector2i.ZERO
+		src.use_texture_padding = true

([] = any) templates which of the asset's templates it applies to ([] = any) friends only while you're Friendly or better with one of these empires ([] = any) chapter_min / chapter_max main-story chapters (stage numbers; -1 = no limit) chance 0-1: how often it's used where it matches priority higher wins over lower when several match pick(kind, context, seed) returns the look to use (or {} for the default). (Moved from scripts/themes.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,171 @@ 
+class_name Themes
+## Named look presets for every customisable asset (buildings,
+## planets, suns, nebulae, the GUI), saved in data/themes.json, each with
+## rules saying where and when the game uses it:
+##   enabled      false: never picked (kept for later)
+##   systems      star systems it may appear in ([] = any)
+##   owners       empires whose space (sector) it may appear in ([] = any)
+##   planets      planets (surfaces) it may appear on ([] = any)
+##   states       system conditions: boom, famine, civil_unrest... ([] = any)
+##   templates    which of the asset's templates it applies to ([] = any)
+##   friends      only while you're Friendly or better with one of these empires
+##                ([] = any)
+##   chapter_min / chapter_max   main-story chapters (stage numbers; -1 = no limit)
+##   chance       0-1: how often it's used where it matches
+##   priority     higher wins over lower when several match
+## pick(kind, context, seed) returns the look to use (or {} for the default).
+
+const FILE := "res://data/themes.json"
+const KINDS := ["building", "planet", "star", "nebula", "asteroid", "gui"]
+const RULE_DEFAULTS := {"enabled": true, "systems": [], "owners": [], "planets": [], "states": [], "templates": [],
+	"friends": [], "chapter_min": -1, "chapter_max": -1, "chance": 1.0, "priority": 0}
+
+static var _data := {}
+static var _loaded := false
+## The main story's current stage (the quest runner keeps it up to date).
+static var chapter := -1
+
+
+static func _load() -> void:
+	if _loaded:
+		return
+	_loaded = true
+	_data = DataFiles.read(FILE)
+	if not _data.has("presets"):
+		_data = {"presets": []}
+
+
+static func reload() -> void:
+	_loaded = false
+	_load()
+
+
+## Every preset of a kind: [{name, kind, look, rules}, ...].
+static func presets(kind: String) -> Array:
+	_load()
+	return (_data["presets"] as Array).filter(func(p): return p.get("kind") == kind)
+
+
+static func find(kind: String, name: String) -> Dictionary:
+	for p in presets(kind):
+		if p.get("name") == name:
+			return p
+	return {}
+
+
+## Saves (or replaces) a named preset; returns the file written.
+static func save_preset(kind: String, name: String, look: Dictionary, rules: Dictionary) -> String:
+	_load()
+	var list: Array = _data["presets"]
+	for i in range(list.size() - 1, -1, -1):
+		if list[i].get("kind") == kind and list[i].get("name") == name:
+			list.remove_at(i)
+	var r := RULE_DEFAULTS.duplicate(true)
+	r.merge(rules, true)
+	list.append({"name": name, "kind": kind, "look": encode(look), "rules": r})
+	return DataFiles.write(FILE, _data)
+
+
+static func delete_preset(kind: String, name: String) -> String:
+	_load()
+	_data["presets"] = (_data["presets"] as Array).filter(func(p): return not (p.get("kind") == kind and p.get("name") == name))
+	return DataFiles.write(FILE, _data)
+
+
+## A preset's look as values (colours and vectors decoded).
+static func look_of(preset: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	return decode(preset.get("look", {}))
+
+
+static func rules_of(preset: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	var r := RULE_DEFAULTS.duplicate(true)
+	r.merge(preset.get("rules", {}), true)
+	return r
+
+
+## Where we are now: {system, owner, state, planet, friends (empires that like you), chapter}.
+static func context(planet := "") -> Dictionary:
+	var sys: String = Galaxy.current_system
+	return {"system": sys, "owner": Galaxy.owner_of(sys), "state": Galaxy.state_of(sys), "planet": planet,
+		"friends": Galaxy.MAJOR.filter(func(e): return Galaxy.standing(e) in ["Friendly", "Allied"]), "chapter": chapter}
+
+
+## True if a preset's rules allow it in this context (template: the asset's).
+static func matches(rules: Dictionary, ctx: Dictionary, template := "") -> bool:
+	var r := RULE_DEFAULTS.duplicate(true)
+	r.merge(rules, true)
+	if not bool(r["enabled"]):
+		return false
+	for pair in [["systems", "system"], ["owners", "owner"], ["planets", "planet"], ["states", "state"]]:
+		var allowed: Array = r[pair[0]]
+		if not allowed.is_empty() and not allowed.has(ctx.get(pair[1], "")):
+			return false
+	var fr: Array = r["friends"]
+	if not fr.is_empty() and not fr.any(func(e): return e in ctx.get("friends", [])):
+		return false
+	var tl: Array = r["templates"]
+	if not tl.is_empty() and template != "" and not tl.has(template):
+		return false
+	var ch := int(ctx.get("chapter", -1))
+	if int(r["chapter_min"]) >= 0 and ch < int(r["chapter_min"]):
+		return false
+	if int(r["chapter_max"]) >= 0 and ch > int(r["chapter_max"]):
+		return false
+	return true
+
+
+## The look the game should use for an asset of `kind` here ({} = its own).
+## Among matching presets the highest priority wins; `seed` makes the
+## chance roll and ties stable (the same NPC keeps its look).
+static func pick(kind: String, ctx: Dictionary, seed := 0, template := "") -> Dictionary:
+	var best: Array = []
+	var best_p := -INF
+	for p in presets(kind):
+		var r := rules_of(p)
+		if not matches(r, ctx, template):
+			continue
+		var roll := float(absi(hash([p.get("name"), seed])) % 10000) / 10000.0
+		if roll >= float(r["chance"]):
+			continue
+		var pr := float(r["priority"])
+		if pr > best_p:
+			best = [p]
+			best_p = pr
+		elif pr == best_p:
+			best.append(p)
+	if best.is_empty():
+		return {}
+	return look_of(best[absi(seed) % best.size()])
+
+
+# --- JSON: colours and vectors as tagged arrays ----------------------------------
+
+static func encode(look: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	var out := {}
+	for k in look:
+		var v = look[k]
+		if v is Color:
+			out[k] = ["color", v.r, v.g, v.b, v.a]
+		elif v is Vector2:
+			out[k] = ["vec2", v.x, v.y]
+		elif v is Vector3:
+			out[k] = ["vec3", v.x, v.y, v.z]
+		elif v is Array or v is Dictionary:
+			continue   # (tags and the like)
+		else:
+			out[k] = v
+	return out
+
+
+static func decode(look: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	var out := {}
+	for k in look:
+		var v = look[k]
+		if v is Array and v.size() > 0 and v[0] is String:
+			match v[0]:
+				"color": out[k] = Color(v[1], v[2], v[3], v[4])
+				"vec2": out[k] = Vector2(v[1], v[2])
+				"vec3": out[k] = Vector3(v[1], v[2], v[3])
+		else:
+			out[k] = v
+	return out

files.explanation: An engine-level service: On a touch screen (a phone or a tablet - the web build): what the mouse and the keyboard do, by hand (autoload "Touch"). A tap is already the left button (Godot's mouse emulation: fly there, walk there, hold to keep going, hold on a rock to cut it). On top of that: - a two-finger tap: the right button where the first finger was (scan a rock, the probe scanner in empty space, the context menu on foot); - a pinch: zoom (the mouse wheel); - two columns of buttons by the left edge for the keys: the menu (Esc), the computer (Tab), the map (M), attack the nearest enemy (F), dock / use (E), zoom in and out - between the status bars and the event log. Shown only with a touch screen (or `forced`: tests), in play - space and a planet's surface - and not while a menu covers the game (they have their own Close buttons). (Moved from scripts/touch_controls.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,151 @@ 
+class_name TouchControls
+extends CanvasLayer
+## On a touch screen (a phone or a tablet - the web build): what the mouse and
+## the keyboard do, by hand (autoload "Touch"). A tap is already the left
+## button (Godot's mouse emulation: fly there, walk there, hold to keep going,
+## hold on a rock to cut it). On top of that:
+##   - a two-finger tap: the right button where the first finger was (scan a
+##     rock, the probe scanner in empty space, the context menu on foot);
+##   - a pinch: zoom (the mouse wheel);
+##   - two columns of buttons by the left edge for the keys: the menu (Esc), the
+##     computer (Tab), the map (M), attack the nearest enemy (F), dock / use
+##     (E), zoom in and out - between the status bars and the event log.
+## Shown only with a touch screen (or `forced`: tests), in play - space and a
+## planet's surface - and not while a menu covers the game (they have their
+## own Close buttons).
+
+const BUTTONS := [["MENU", "pause"], ["COMPUTER", "computer"], ["MAP", "sector_map"], ["ATTACK", "attack"], ["DOCK", "dock"]]
+## Pixels a pinch has to open or close by for one step of zoom.
+const PINCH_STEP := 48.0
+## A two-finger tap: both down for less than this, neither moving more than TAP_SLOP.
+const TAP_TIME := 0.35
+const TAP_SLOP := 24.0
+
+var forced := false
+var _col: GridContainer
+var _touches := {}     # finger index -> position (the viewport's)
+var _starts := {}      # finger index -> [position, time]
+var _pinch_d := 0.0
+var _two_tap := false
+var _check := 0.0
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	layer = 60   # (over the HUD; the menus hide it)
+	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	# Two columns by the left edge, between the status bars and the event log
+	# (the right side has the tutorial's icon and the missions).
+	_col = GridContainer.new()
+	_col.name = "Buttons"
+	_col.columns = 2
+	_col.add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", 10)
+	_col.add_theme_constant_override("v_separation", 10)
+	_col.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_CENTER_LEFT)
+	_col.grow_horizontal = Control.GROW_DIRECTION_END
+	_col.grow_vertical = Control.GROW_DIRECTION_BOTH
+	_col.offset_left = 18
+	_col.modulate = Color(1, 1, 1, 0.8)
+	for b in BUTTONS:
+		_col.add_child(_button(b[0], _act.bind(b[1])))
+	_col.add_child(_button("ZOOM +", _wheel.bind(MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP)))
+	_col.add_child(_button("ZOOM -", _wheel.bind(MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN)))
+	add_child(_col)
+	visible = false
+
+
+func _button(text: String, cb: Callable, min_size := Vector2(154, 64)) -> Button:
+	var b := UI.button(text, cb, 20)
+	b.custom_minimum_size = min_size
+	b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	return b
+
+
+## A touch screen here? (the web build on a phone or a tablet; a laptop's touch screen too)
+static func available() -> bool:
+	return DisplayServer.is_touchscreen_available()
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_check -= delta
+	if _check > 0.0:
+		return
+	_check = 0.25
+	visible = (forced or available()) and in_play() and Keybinds.active_menu() == null and not UI.esc_menu_open()
+
+
+## Space or a planet's surface (not the title screen, Talos, a loading screen).
+func in_play() -> bool:
+	var s := get_tree().current_scene
+	if s == null or s.get_script() == null:
+		return false
+	var p: String = s.get_script().resource_path
+	return p.ends_with("/main.gd") or p.ends_with("/planet_surface.gd")
+
+
+## A key's action, pressed and let go.
+func _act(id: String) -> void:
+	for down in [true, false]:
+		var e := InputEventAction.new()
+		e.action = id
+		e.pressed = down
+		Input.parse_input_event(e)
+
+
+## The mouse wheel at the middle of the screen (zoom).
+func _wheel(button: MouseButton) -> void:
+	var vp := get_viewport()
+	_click(vp.get_visible_rect().size * 0.5, button)
+
+
+## A mouse button pressed and let go at `at` (the viewport's coordinates).
+func _click(at: Vector2, button: MouseButton) -> void:
+	var win := get_viewport().get_final_transform() * at   # (events come in as the window's)
+	for down in [true, false]:
+		var e := InputEventMouseButton.new()
+		e.button_index = button
+		e.pressed = down
+		e.position = win
+		e.global_position = win
+		Input.parse_input_event(e)
+
+
+func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
+	if not (forced or available()):
+		return
+	if event is InputEventScreenTouch:
+		var now := Time.get_ticks_msec() / 1000.0
+		if event.pressed:
+			_touches[event.index] = event.position
+			_starts[event.index] = [event.position, now]
+			if _touches.size() == 2:
+				_pinch_d = _span()
+				_two_tap = true
+			elif _touches.size() > 2:
+				_two_tap = false
+		else:
+			if _two_tap and _touches.size() == 2:
+				var first: int = _touches.keys().min()
+				var quick := true
+				for i in _starts:
+					quick = quick and now - float(_starts[i][1]) <= TAP_TIME
+				if quick:
+					_click(_starts[first][0], MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT)
+			_two_tap = false
+			_touches.erase(event.index)
+			_starts.erase(event.index)
+	elif event is InputEventScreenDrag and _touches.has(event.index):
+		_touches[event.index] = event.position
+		if _starts.has(event.index) and event.position.distance_to(_starts[event.index][0]) > TAP_SLOP:
+			_two_tap = false
+		if _touches.size() == 2:
+			var d := _span()
+			if absf(d - _pinch_d) >= PINCH_STEP:
+				var mid: Vector2 = (_touches.values()[0] + _touches.values()[1]) * 0.5
+				_click(mid, MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP if d > _pinch_d else MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN)
+				_pinch_d = d
+				_two_tap = false
+
+
+func _span() -> float:
+	var v := _touches.values()
+	return (v[0] as Vector2).distance_to(v[1]) if v.size() >= 2 else 0.0

files.explanation: An engine-level service: Autoload "Voice": spoken dialogue. Every story line is recorded with Piper (neural text to speech, offline) by tools/voice_lines.py, one voice per character, as res://voices/lines/<key>.ogg - key: the first 16 hex digits of sha1("<speaker>|<the line without BBCode>"). Saying a line plays its own recording: Voice.speak("Then the thread is in your hands.", "Kilon Alios") Voice.stop() A line with no recording (edited since, or never recorded) is silent - run tools/voice_lines.py again (test_audio checks every quest line has one). The dialogue box speaks each line as it shows it. Plays on the "Voice" bus (Settings.voice_volume), also while the game is paused. (Moved from scripts/voice.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,75 @@ 
+extends Node
+## Autoload "Voice": spoken dialogue. Every story line is recorded with
+## Piper (neural text to speech, offline) by tools/voice_lines.py, one voice
+## per character, as res://voices/lines/<key>.ogg - key: the first 16 hex
+## digits of sha1("<speaker>|<the line without BBCode>"). Saying a line plays
+## its own recording:
+##
+##   Voice.speak("Then the thread is in your hands.", "Kilon Alios")
+##   Voice.stop()
+##
+## A line with no recording (edited since, or never recorded) is silent - run
+## tools/voice_lines.py again (test_audio checks every quest line has one).
+## The dialogue box speaks each line as it shows it. Plays on the "Voice"
+## bus (Settings.voice_volume), also while the game is paused.
+
+const DIR := "res://voices/lines/"
+const BUS := "Voice"
+
+var _player: AudioStreamPlayer
+var speaking := ""                  # the key of the line being spoken ("" none)
+static var _bb := RegEx.create_from_string("\\[[^\\]]*\\]")
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	if AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS) < 0:
+		AudioServer.add_bus()
+		var i := AudioServer.bus_count - 1
+		AudioServer.set_bus_name(i, BUS)
+		AudioServer.set_bus_send(i, "Master")
+	_player = AudioStreamPlayer.new()
+	_player.bus = BUS
+	_player.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	_player.finished.connect(func(): speaking = "")
+	add_child(_player)
+	apply_volume()
+
+
+## The Voice bus at Settings.voice_volume (0 = silent).
+func apply_volume() -> void:
+	var i := AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS)
+	if i < 0:
+		return
+	var v: float = Settings.voice_volume
+	AudioServer.set_bus_mute(i, v <= 0.001)
+	AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(i, linear_to_db(maxf(v, 0.001)))
+
+
+## The recording's key for a line (as tools/voice_lines.py names it).
+static func key(text: String, speaker: String) -> String:
+	var plain := _bb.sub(text, "", true).strip_edges()
+	return ("%s|%s" % [speaker, plain]).sha1_text().substr(0, 16)
+
+
+## The recording of a line (null if it has none).
+static func recording(text: String, speaker: String) -> AudioStream:
+	var path := DIR + key(text, speaker) + ".ogg"
+	return load(path) if ResourceLoader.exists(path) else null
+
+
+## Speaks a line (stopping whatever was being said); silent if it has no recording.
+func speak(text: String, speaker: String) -> void:
+	stop()
+	var st := recording(text, speaker)
+	if st == null:
+		return
+	speaking = key(text, speaker)
+	_player.stream = st
+	_player.play()
+
+
+func stop() -> void:
+	if _player and _player.playing:
+		_player.stop()
+	speaking = ""

+	# Right: the selected asset.
+	var right := VBoxContainer.new()
+	right.custom_minimum_size.x = 400
+	right.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 8)
+	row.add_child(right)
+	var pv := PanelContainer.new()
+	var pvs := StyleBoxFlat.new()
+	pvs.bg_color = Color(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.55)
+	pvs.border_color = Color(NeonTheme.CYAN, 0.35)
+	pvs.set_border_width_all(1)
+	pv.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", pvs)
+	pv.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(400, 320)
+	right.add_child(pv)
+	_preview = TextureRect.new()
+	_preview.expand_mode = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
+	_preview.stretch_mode = TextureRect.STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED
+	_preview.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR
+	pv.add_child(_preview)
+	_swatch = _disc_control(Color(0, 0, 0, 0))
+	pv.add_child(_swatch)
+	_title = UI.label("", 22, Color.WHITE)
+	_title.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
+	right.add_child(_title)
+	_sub = UI.label("", 15, NeonTheme.HEAD)
+	right.add_child(_sub)
+	_info = UI.label("", 14, UI.TEXT_DIM)
+	_info.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
+	right.add_child(_info)
+	_file = UI.label("", 12, Color(UI.TEXT_DIM, 0.8))
+	_file.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_ARBITRARY
+	right.add_child(_file)
+	_live = UI.button("View live", _open_live, 17)
+	_live.custom_minimum_size.y = 42
+	_live.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("View live", "Double-click a card",
+		"Opens the Library's live room with this asset in it: animated as in the game - and planets, suns and nebulae editable there.")
+	right.add_child(_live)
+	if first:
+		first.select(0)
+		_on_tree()
+
+
+## A category's icon and its tint: [EditorIcons name, colour].
+static func category_icon(cat: String) -> Array:
+	var white := Color.WHITE
+	var tint := {"forest": Color(0.5, 0.95, 0.5), "ice": Color(0.6, 0.85, 1.0), "volcanic": Color(1.0, 0.5, 0.3), "gas giant": Color(1.0, 0.8, 0.45)}
+	for k in tint:
+		if cat.to_lower().contains(k):
+			return ["terrain" if cat.begins_with("Terrain") else "neutral", tint[k]]
+	return [{"Ships": "ships", "Ship": "ship", "Pilot": "characters", "Stations": "stations", "Station": "stations", "Characters": "characters", "Portraits": "npc",
+		"Buildings": "buildings", "Furniture": "prop", "Effects": "effects", "Creatures of myth": "enemy",
+		"Bosses": "enemy", "Planets": "planets", "Suns": "suns", "Nebulae": "nebulae", "Asteroids": "asteroid",
+		"Jump gates": "star_tool", "Skies": "eye", "Widgets": "gui", "Interface": "gui", "Others": "neutral"}.get(cat, "zoo"),
+		Color(1.0, 0.75, 0.5) if cat == "Bosses" else white]
+
+
+## A small coloured dot (the owners' tree).
+static func _dot(c: Color) -> Texture2D:
+	var img := Image.create(14, 14, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
+	for y in 14:
+		for x in 14:
+			var d := Vector2(x - 6.5, y - 6.5).length()
+			img.set_pixel(x, y, Color(c, clampf(6.0 - d, 0.0, 1.0)))
+	return ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)
+
+
+## A shaded disc in a colour (procedural assets: planets, suns, nebulae, asteroids).
+static func _disc_control(c: Color) -> Control:
+	var d := Control.new()
+	d.set_meta("color", c)
+	d.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	d.draw.connect(func():
+		var col: Color = d.get_meta("color")
+		if col.a <= 0.0:
+			return
+		var r := minf(d.size.x, d.size.y) * 0.38
+		var ctr := d.size / 2.0
+		for i in 6:
+			d.draw_circle(ctr, r * (1.35 - i * 0.05), Color(col, 0.04))
+		d.draw_circle(ctr, r, col.darkened(0.45))
+		d.draw_circle(ctr - Vector2(r, r) * 0.2, r * 0.78, col)
+		d.draw_circle(ctr - Vector2(r, r) * 0.38, r * 0.3, col.lightened(0.3)))
+	return d
+
+
+func _on_tree() -> void:
+	var it := _tree.get_selected()
+	if it == null:
+		return
+	var md: Dictionary = it.get_metadata(0)
+	_search.text = ""
+	var entries := []
+	var head := ""
+	if md.has("category"):
+		entries = md["category"]["entries"]
+		head = "%s  ·  %s  (%d)" % [md["owner"]["name"].to_upper(), md["category"]["name"].to_upper(), entries.size()]
+	else:
+		for c in md["owner"]["categories"]:
+			entries.append_array(c["entries"])
+		head = "%s  ·  EVERYTHING  (%d)" % [md["owner"]["name"].to_upper(), entries.size()]
+	_show(entries, head)
+
+
+func _show_search() -> void:
+	var q := _search.text.strip_edges().to_lower()
+	if q == "":
+		_on_tree()
+		return
+	var hits := []
+	for t in AssetCatalog.all_entries():
+		var e: Dictionary = t[2]
+		if q in str(e["title"]).to_lower() or q in str(e["key"]).to_lower() or q in str(t[0]["name"]).to_lower():
+			hits.append(e)
+	_show(hits, "SEARCH  ·  \"%s\"  (%d)" % [_search.text.strip_edges(), hits.size()])
+
+
+## Shows these entries as cards (the first one selected).
+func _show(entries: Array, head: String) -> void:
+	_head.text = head
+	UI.clear(_grid)
+	_cards = {}
+	_cur = entries
+	for e in entries:
+		_grid.add_child(_card(e))
+	_scroll.scroll_vertical = 0
+	if not entries.is_empty():
+		select(entries[0])
+	else:
+		select({})
+
+
+func _card(e: Dictionary) -> Button:
+	var b := Button.new()
+	b.toggle_mode = true
+	b.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(160, 186)
+	b.tooltip_text = "%s\n%s" % [e["title"], e["info"]]
+	b.pressed.connect(func(): select(e))
+	b.gui_input.connect(func(ev):
+		if ev is InputEventMouseButton and ev.double_click and ev.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT:
+			select(e)
+			_open_live())
+	var v := VBoxContainer.new()
+	v.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+	v.offset_left = 6
+	v.offset_right = -6
+	v.offset_top = 6
+	v.offset_bottom = -6
+	v.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	b.add_child(v)
+	var tex := AssetCatalog.texture(e)
+	if tex:
+		var tr := TextureRect.new()
+		tr.texture = tex
+		tr.expand_mode = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
+		tr.stretch_mode = TextureRect.STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED
+		tr.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(148, 132)
+		tr.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+		v.add_child(tr)
+	else:
+		var d := _disc_control(e["swatch"] if e["swatch"].a > 0.0 else Color(0.4, 0.42, 0.5))
+		d.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(148, 132)
+		v.add_child(d)
+	var l := UI.label(e["title"], 13, Color.WHITE)
+	l.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
+	l.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
+	l.max_lines_visible = 2
+	l.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	v.add_child(l)
+	_cards[e["key"]] = b
+	return b
+
+
+## Selects an entry: its card lit, its preview and details on the right.
+func select(e: Dictionary) -> void:
+	_sel = e
+	for k in _cards:
+		_cards[k].set_pressed_no_signal(not e.is_empty() and k == e["key"])
+	if e.is_empty():
+		_preview.texture = null
+		_swatch.set_meta("color", Color(0, 0, 0, 0))
+		_swatch.queue_redraw()
+		_title.text = "Nothing here"
+		_sub.text = ""
+		_info.text = ""
+		_file.text = ""
+		_live.disabled = true
+		return
+	var tex := AssetCatalog.texture(e)
+	_preview.texture = tex
+	_swatch.set_meta("color", e["swatch"] if tex == null else Color(0, 0, 0, 0))
+	_swatch.queue_redraw()
+	_title.text = e["title"]
+	var size_txt := ("  ·  %d x %d px" % [tex.get_width(), tex.get_height()]) if tex else ""
+	_sub.text = str(e["sub"]) + size_txt
+	_info.text = e["info"]
+	var t: String = e["tex"]
+	_file.text = t if t.begins_with("res://") else (("data/sprites/%s.png" % t) if t != "" and not t.begins_with("type:") else "")
+	_live.disabled = str(e["room"]) == ""
+	_live.text = "View live  ·  %s" % str(e["room"]).capitalize() if not _live.disabled else "No live room"
+
+
+func selected() -> Dictionary:
+	return _sel
+
+
+func _open_live() -> void:
+	if not _sel.is_empty() and str(_sel["room"]) != "":
+		view_live.emit(_sel["room"], _sel["spot"])
+
+
+## Shows a category by its owner id and name (tests, LiveLink).
+func open(owner_id: String, category := "") -> bool:
+	var it := _tree.get_root().get_first_child()
+	while it:
+		var md: Dictionary = it.get_metadata(0)
+		if md["owner"]["id"] == owner_id:
+			if category == "":
+				it.select(0)
+				_on_tree()
+				return true
+			var c := it.get_first_child()
+			while c:
+				if c.get_metadata(0)["category"]["name"] == category:
+					it.collapsed = false
+					c.select(0)
+					_on_tree()
+					return true
+				c = c.get_next()
+		it = it.get_next()
+	return false
+
+
+func shown() -> Array:
+	return _cur
