files.explanation: Talos, the game's editor: The docs books (data/docs/*.md: the Talos manual, the pilot's guide, the tutorial), organised like books: chapters ("# id | Title", then an introduction) holding sections ("## id | Title"), written in a small Markdown subset - **bold**, `code`, "- " lists, [text](doc:id) links. Read here, shown in the Archive (EditorDocs.open() opens it at a section) and linked from every tooltip (PinTips). Chapter pages have the ids "ch:<chapter id>". (Moved from scripts/editor_docs.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,234 @@ 
+class_name EditorDocs
+## The docs books (data/docs/*.md: the Talos manual, the pilot's guide, the
+## tutorial), organised like books: chapters ("# id | Title", then an
+## introduction) holding sections ("## id | Title"), written in a small
+## Markdown subset - **bold**, `code`, "- " lists, [text](doc:id) links. Read
+## here, shown in the Archive (EditorDocs.open() opens it at a section) and
+## linked from every tooltip (PinTips). Chapter pages have the ids "ch:<chapter id>".
+
+const FILE := "res://data/docs/editor.md"
+## The player's guide (same format), for the game's own screens.
+const GAME := "res://data/docs/game.md"
+## The tutorial: lessons, in the order you need them.
+const TUTORIAL := "res://data/docs/tutorial.md"
+static var _file := FILE            # the book in use (see use())
+static var _keywords: Array = []    # [keyword, section]: tooltip titles a section explains
+static var _sections := {}          # id -> [title, markdown]
+static var _order: Array = []
+static var _chapters: Array = []    # [{id, title, intro, sections: [ids]}]
+static var _chapter_of := {}        # section id -> chapter index
+
+## Which section a tooltip's title points to: [keyword, section] (first match wins).
+const TOPICS := [
+	["Paint terrain", "level-tools"], ["Draw building", "level-tools"], ["Wall:", "level-tools"], ["Place ", "level-tools"],
+	["Erase", "level-tools"],
+	["Library", "zoo"], ["Save layout", "layouts"], ["Revert to generated", "layouts"],
+	["Brush", "level-tools"], ["Kind", "level-tools"], ["Exit the level editor", "level-editor"],
+	["Save to file", "data-editor"], ["Reload from file", "data-editor"], ["Back to the main menu", "data-editor"],
+	["Dialogue", "dialogue"], ["Speaker", "dialogue"], ["Line", "dialogue"], ["Add line", "dialogue"], ["Quest stages", "dialogue"],
+	["Quest", "quest"], ["Chapter", "quest"], ["Lore", "lore"], ["Interactions", "interactions"], ["citizen", "interactions"],
+	["Minoan words", "interactions"], ["Translation", "interactions"], ["Sprites", "sprites"], ["sprites", "sprites"],
+	["Characters", "zoo"], ["Ships", "zoo"], ["Stations", "zoo"], ["Planets", "zoo"], ["Buildings", "zoo"], ["Effects", "zoo"],
+]
+
+
+## Switches to another book (a docs file); each is read once and kept (the
+## Archive reads several in turn).
+static var _books := {}             # file -> [sections, order, chapters, chapter_of, keywords]
+static func use(file: String) -> void:
+	if file == _file:
+		return
+	if not _sections.is_empty():
+		_books[_file] = [_sections, _order, _chapters, _chapter_of, _keywords]
+	_file = file
+	if _books.has(file):
+		var b: Array = _books[file]
+		_sections = b[0]
+		_order = b[1]
+		_chapters = b[2]
+		_chapter_of = b[3]
+		_keywords = b[4]
+		return
+	_sections = {}
+	_order = []
+	_chapters = []
+	_chapter_of = {}
+	_keywords = []
+
+
+static func book() -> String:
+	return _file
+
+
+static func _load() -> void:
+	if not _sections.is_empty():
+		return
+	var text := FileAccess.get_file_as_string(_file)
+	var id := ""
+	var body := PackedStringArray()
+	for line in text.split("\n"):
+		if line.begins_with("# ") and line.contains("|"):   # a chapter
+			_flush(id, body)
+			var head := line.substr(2).split("|", true, 1)
+			id = "ch:" + head[0].strip_edges()
+			_chapters.append({"id": id, "title": head[1].strip_edges(), "intro": "", "sections": []})
+			body = PackedStringArray()
+		elif line.begins_with("## "):
+			_flush(id, body)
+			# "## id | Title | keywords: a, b" - the keywords are tooltip titles it explains.
+			var head := line.substr(3).split("|")
+			id = head[0].strip_edges()
+			_sections[id] = [head[1].strip_edges() if head.size() > 1 else id, ""]
+			if head.size() > 2 and head[2].strip_edges().begins_with("keywords:"):
+				for kw in head[2].strip_edges().substr(9).split(","):
+					if kw.strip_edges() != "":
+						_keywords.append([kw.strip_edges(), id])
+			_order.append(id)
+			if not _chapters.is_empty():
+				_chapters[-1]["sections"].append(id)
+				_chapter_of[id] = _chapters.size() - 1
+			body = PackedStringArray()
+		elif id != "":
+			body.append(line)
+	_flush(id, body)
+
+
+static func ids() -> Array:
+	_load()
+	return _order
+
+
+## Stores the text read for a chapter introduction or a section.
+static func _flush(id: String, body: PackedStringArray) -> void:
+	if id.begins_with("ch:"):
+		_chapters[-1]["intro"] = "\n".join(body).strip_edges()
+	elif id != "":
+		_sections[id][1] = "\n".join(body).strip_edges()
+
+
+static func chapters() -> Array:
+	_load()
+	return _chapters
+
+
+static func _chapter(id: String) -> Dictionary:
+	for c in _chapters:
+		if c["id"] == id:
+			return c
+	return {}
+
+
+static func title(id: String) -> String:
+	_load()
+	if id.begins_with("ch:"):
+		return _chapter(id).get("title", id)
+	return _sections[id][0] if _sections.has(id) else id
+
+
+## "2.3" for a section, "2" for a chapter ("" if not in a chapter).
+static func number(id: String) -> String:
+	_load()
+	for i in _chapters.size():
+		if _chapters[i]["id"] == id:
+			return str(i + 1)
+	if _chapter_of.has(id):
+		var ci: int = _chapter_of[id]
+		return "%d.%d" % [ci + 1, _chapters[ci]["sections"].find(id) + 1]
+	return ""
+
+
+## "2.3  Title".
+static func numbered(id: String) -> String:
+	var n := number(id)
+	return (n + "  " if n != "" else "") + title(id)
+
+
+static func has(id: String) -> bool:
+	_load()
+	return _sections.has(id) or not _chapter(id).is_empty()
+
+
+## The chapter a section belongs to ("" if none).
+static func chapter_of(id: String) -> String:
+	_load()
+	return _chapters[_chapter_of[id]]["id"] if _chapter_of.has(id) else ""
+
+
+## Reading order: every chapter page, then its sections.
+static func reading_order() -> Array:
+	_load()
+	var out := []
+	for c in _chapters:
+		out.append(c["id"])
+		out.append_array(c["sections"])
+	return out
+
+
+## The section a tooltip (by its title) is about ("" if none matches).
+static func topic(tip_title: String) -> String:
+	_load()
+	for t in _keywords:
+		if tip_title.contains(t[0]):
+			return t[1]
+	if _file != FILE:
+		return ""
+	for t in TOPICS:
+		if tip_title.contains(t[0]):
+			return t[1]
+	return ""
+
+
+## Markdown subset -> BBCode.
+static func to_bbcode(md: String) -> String:
+	var out := PackedStringArray()
+	var re_b := RegEx.create_from_string("\\*\\*(.+?)\\*\\*")
+	var re_c := RegEx.create_from_string("`([^`]+)`")
+	var re_l := RegEx.create_from_string("\\[([^\\]]+)\\]\\((doc:[a-z0-9-]+)\\)")
+	for line in md.split("\n"):
+		# Code spans first, their brackets shown literally.
+		var l := ""
+		var last := 0
+		for m in re_c.search_all(line):
+			l += line.substr(last, m.get_start() - last)
+			l += "[color=#ffd27a][code]" + m.get_string(1).replace("[", "[lb]") + "[/code][/color]"
+			last = m.get_end()
+		l += line.substr(last)
+		l = re_b.sub(l, "[b]$1[/b]", true)
+		l = re_l.sub(l, "[color=#7fd6ff][url=$2]$1[/url][/color]", true)
+		if l.begins_with("- "):
+			l = "  •  " + l.substr(2)
+		out.append(l)
+	return "\n".join(out)
+
+
+static func body(id: String) -> String:
+	_load()
+	if id.begins_with("ch:"):
+		var c := _chapter(id)
+		var lines := [to_bbcode(c.get("intro", "")), "", "[b]In this chapter:[/b]"]
+		for s in c.get("sections", []):
+			lines.append("  %s   [color=#7fd6ff][url=doc:%s]%s[/url][/color]" % [number(s), s, title(s)])
+		return "\n".join(lines)
+	return to_bbcode(_sections[id][1]) if _sections.has(id) else ""
+
+
+## Searchable text of a page.
+static func text_of(id: String) -> String:
+	_load()
+	if id.begins_with("ch:"):
+		var c := _chapter(id)
+		return c.get("title", "") + " " + c.get("intro", "")
+	return title(id) + " " + (_sections[id][1] if _sections.has(id) else "")
+
+
+## Opens the Archive (the one window for all the game's books) at a section
+## of book `file` (FILE, the editor's; GAME, the player's guide; TUTORIAL).
+static func open(owner: Node, id := "", file := "") -> void:
+	if file == "":
+		file = _file
+	var b: String = {FILE: "talos", GAME: "guide", TUTORIAL: "tutorial"}.get(file, "guide")
+	if id == "":
+		id = "overview" if file == FILE else "start"
+	use(file)
+	# (loaded now, not named: this class is used before the autoloads exist - by -s scripts too)
+	load("res://scripts/ui/archive.gd").open(owner, b, b + "/" + id if has(id) else "")

@@ -1,0 +1,206 @@ 
+extends Control
+## Talos, the editor (main menu > Talos): the host of all its tools, over the
+## title screen's starfield. The data editor (DevMode: quest dialogue,
+## chapters, lore, citizens, sprites) is here from the start; the other tools
+## (Scenarios, Library, SVG, Patcher - their own scenes) are built the first
+## time you open one and then kept: switching (the rail, TalosNav) only
+## shows one and hides the rest - nothing is rebuilt, nothing is lost, so
+## switching never asks about unsaved changes. Leaving Talos (Exit, or Esc in
+## the data editor) does, tool by tool (exit()).
+
+const MENU_SCENE := "res://scenes/ui/main_menu.tscn"
+## Where a screen not showing waits (x, px): far off to the side.
+const PARKED := 100000.0
+
+var editor: DevMode
+## The tools built so far: id -> their scene's root.
+var tools := {}
+## The tool showing ("" - the data editor).
+var current := ""
+var _sky: CanvasLayer
+var _dim: ColorRect
+## Opened over a running game (SaveGame.open_talos): in a CanvasLayer of
+## its own above the game; leaving closes it (TalosNav.leave).
+var overlay := false
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	add_to_group("talos_host")
+	NeonTheme.set_empire("")
+	Galaxy.active = false
+	set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+	# (the host itself takes no mouse: over the Library - a world, not a Control -
+	# a full-screen STOP here swallowed every press and drag meant for its view)
+	mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	_sky = CanvasLayer.new()
+	_sky.layer = -1
+	add_child(_sky)
+	if overlay:   # (over a game: an opaque ground under every tool - the Library's world too - so nothing of the game shows through)
+		var ground_layer := CanvasLayer.new()
+		ground_layer.layer = -3
+		add_child(ground_layer)
+		var ground := ColorRect.new()
+		ground.color = Color(0.01, 0.0, 0.03)
+		ground.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+		ground.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+		ground_layer.add_child(ground)
+	var stars: Node2D = preload("res://scripts/ui/starfield.gd").new()
+	stars.drift = Vector2(-12, 4)
+	_sky.add_child(stars)
+	_dim = ColorRect.new()
+	_dim.color = Color(0.02, 0.0, 0.06, 0.55)
+	_dim.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+	_dim.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	add_child(_dim)
+	# The data editor a piece a frame (all in this frame: a 35-40 ms frame as
+	# Talos opened over the game): itself, its frame, then its page. A tool
+	# asked for meanwhile (the rail, Exit) waits for it (_wanted). Headless
+	# (tests): all at once.
+	if not await _next_piece():
+		return
+	editor = DevMode.new()
+	add_child(editor)
+	# Dialogue previews play in a dialogue box of their own.
+	var box: Control = preload("res://scripts/ui/dialogue.gd").new()
+	box.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS   # (it pauses the tree while it plays)
+	add_child(box)
+	editor.dialogue = box
+	editor.closed.connect(func(): TalosNav.leave(get_tree()))
+	editor.svg_requested.connect(show_tool.bind("svg"))
+	editor.patcher_requested.connect(show_tool.bind("patcher"))
+	if not await _next_piece():
+		return
+	editor._build()
+	if not await _next_piece():
+		return
+	editor.open()
+	PinTips.install(editor, "data-editor")
+	_editor_ready = true
+	if _wanted != "":
+		show_tool(_wanted)
+		_wanted = ""
+
+
+## On to the next frame (not headless); false if Talos closed meanwhile.
+func _next_piece() -> bool:
+	if DisplayServer.get_name() != "headless":
+		await get_tree().process_frame
+	return is_inside_tree()
+
+
+## The data editor's made (_ready: a piece a frame); a tool asked for before that.
+var _editor_ready := false
+var _wanted := ""
+
+
+## Shows tool `id` (a data-editor page, a tool, or "menu": leave Talos).
+func show_tool(id: String) -> void:
+	if not _editor_ready:
+		_wanted = id   # (shown once the editor's made)
+		return
+	if id == "menu":
+		exit()
+		return
+	if id in TalosNav.PAGES:
+		_activate("")
+		editor.show_tab(TalosNav.PAGES.find(id))
+		return
+	if not TalosNav.SCENES.has(id):
+		return
+	if not tools.has(id):
+		var n: Node = TalosNav.scene(TalosNav.SCENES[id]).instantiate()
+		tools[id] = n
+		add_child(n)
+	_activate(id)
+
+
+func _activate(id: String) -> void:
+	current = id
+	for t in tools:
+		if t != id:
+			_set_on(tools[t], false)
+	if id != "":
+		_set_on(tools[id], true)
+	_set_on(editor, id == "")
+	# The Library is a world of its own (its camera, its backdrops).
+	var world := id != "" and tools[id] is Node2D
+	_sky.visible = not world
+	_dim.visible = not world
+	if overlay and get_parent() is CanvasLayer:
+		# (over a game: Talos's layer follows the camera only for the Library's
+		# world; the screens stay put whatever the game's camera did)
+		(get_parent() as CanvasLayer).follow_viewport_enabled = world
+	if not world:
+		get_viewport().canvas_transform = Transform2D.IDENTITY
+
+
+## A tool on (shown, running, answering input) or off (hidden and still).
+func _set_on(n: Node, on: bool) -> void:
+	if n.has_meta("talos_off") != on:
+		return   # (already so: hiding twice would forget what was showing)
+	if on:
+		n.remove_meta("talos_off")
+	else:
+		n.set_meta("talos_off", true)
+	if not on:
+		if not n.has_meta("talos_mode"):
+			n.set_meta("talos_mode", n.process_mode)
+		n.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED
+	elif n.has_meta("talos_mode"):
+		n.process_mode = n.get_meta("talos_mode")
+		n.remove_meta("talos_mode")
+	if n is Control:
+		# (parked off to the side rather than hidden: showing a hidden screen
+		# lays out all of it again - ~25 ms for the Scenario Editor - moving
+		# it back, ~1 ms; off screen it isn't drawn and can't be clicked)
+		n.position.x = 0.0 if on else PARKED
+		if on:
+			n.remove_meta("talos_parked")
+		else:
+			n.set_meta("talos_parked", true)
+		if not on and n.get_viewport().gui_get_focus_owner() and n.is_ancestor_of(n.get_viewport().gui_get_focus_owner()):
+			n.get_viewport().gui_release_focus()
+	elif n is CanvasItem:
+		n.visible = on
+	for cl in n.get_children():   # (a tool's layers - its UI, backdrops, tooltips, dialogs - are its own children)
+		if not cl is CanvasLayer:
+			continue
+		if on:
+			cl.visible = cl.get_meta("talos_was_visible", true)
+		else:
+			cl.set_meta("talos_was_visible", cl.visible)
+			cl.visible = false
+	if on and n.has_method("talos_shown"):
+		n.talos_shown()   # (work it put off while it wasn't showing)
+	var cam: Camera2D = n.get("cam") if n.get("cam") is Camera2D else null
+	if cam:
+		cam.enabled = on
+		if on:
+			cam.make_current()
+
+
+## Leaves Talos for the title screen (or the game it was opened from: F8 / the
+## Esc menu - SaveGame.open_talos): every tool with unsaved changes is
+## shown in turn and asks first (save, discard or stay).
+func exit() -> void:
+	if not _editor_ready:
+		_wanted = "menu"
+		return
+	var order: Array = [editor]
+	for t in ["svg", "patcher"]:
+		if tools.has(t):
+			order.append(tools[t])
+	_exit_from(order, 0)
+
+
+func _exit_from(order: Array, i: int) -> void:
+	if i >= order.size():
+		TalosNav.leave(get_tree())   # (the title screen - or the game Talos was opened from)
+		return
+	var n: Node = order[i]
+	var next := _exit_from.bind(order, i + 1)
+	if n.get("dirty") == true and n.has_method("guard"):   # (the Library and Versions have none)
+		show_tool(TalosNav.PAGES[TalosNav.page] if n == editor else tools.find_key(n))
+		n.guard(next)
+	else:
+		next.call()

files.explanation: Talos, the game's editor: Level editor overlay (right-click menu > Level Editor). Works on any "host" scene that provides: editor_title() -> String editor_tools() -> Array of {id, label, options?: Array, brush?: bool, drag?: bool, rect?: bool} editor_apply(tool_id, option, brush, world, phase, start_world) phase: "press", "drag" or "release" editor_rect_polygon(a, b) -> PackedVector2Array (for rect tools) editor_save() -> String, editor_revert() -> String editor_camera() -> Camera2D The game pauses while editing; the camera pans (WASD / arrows / middle drag) and zooms (wheel) freely. (Moved from scripts/level_editor.gd.)

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,313 @@ 
+class_name LevelEditor
+extends Control
+## Level editor overlay (right-click menu > Level Editor). Works on any
+## "host" scene that provides:
+##   editor_title() -> String
+##   editor_tools() -> Array of {id, label, options?: Array, brush?: bool,
+##                               drag?: bool, rect?: bool}
+##   editor_apply(tool_id, option, brush, world, phase, start_world)
+##       phase: "press", "drag" or "release"
+##   editor_rect_polygon(a, b) -> PackedVector2Array   (for rect tools)
+##   editor_save() -> String, editor_revert() -> String
+##   editor_camera() -> Camera2D
+## The game pauses while editing; the camera pans (WASD / arrows / middle
+## drag) and zooms (wheel) freely.
+
+const ACCENT := Color(0.4, 1.0, 0.6)
+const PAN_SPEED := 900.0
+
+var host: Node
+var _tools: Array = []
+var _tool := 0
+var _opt := 0
+var _brush := 1
+var _panel: PanelContainer
+var _tool_buttons: Array = []
+var _options: OptionButton
+var _brush_row: HBoxContainer
+var _status: Label
+var _drag_start: Variant = null
+var _panning := false
+var _cam: Camera2D
+var _cam_saved := {}
+var _paused_by_me := false
+var _built := false
+## Changes since the layout was last saved.
+var dirty := false
+var _brush_slider: HSlider
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	hide()
+	set_anchors_preset(PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+	mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+
+
+func open() -> void:
+	if not _built:
+		_build()
+	_paused_by_me = not get_tree().paused
+	get_tree().paused = true
+	_cam = host.editor_camera()
+	_cam_saved = {"mode": _cam.process_mode, "smooth": _cam.position_smoothing_enabled, "zoom": _cam.zoom, "offset": _cam.offset}
+	_cam.process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	_cam.position_smoothing_enabled = false
+	show()
+	_select_tool(_tool)
+	GameLog.post("[Dev] Level editor opened", "info")
+
+
+## Leaves the editor, asking first about unsaved layout changes.
+func close() -> void:
+	if dirty and visible:
+		UI.unsaved(self, "This map's layout", _save, func(): dirty = false, _close_now)
+		return
+	_close_now()
+
+
+## (Exit without saving keeps the edits on this map until you leave it.)
+func _close_now() -> void:
+	hide()
+	_drag_start = null
+	if _cam:
+		_cam.offset = _cam_saved["offset"]
+		_cam.zoom = _cam_saved["zoom"]
+		_cam.position_smoothing_enabled = _cam_saved["smooth"]
+		_cam.process_mode = _cam_saved["mode"]
+	if _paused_by_me:
+		get_tree().paused = false
+
+
+func _build() -> void:
+	_built = true
+	_tools = host.editor_tools()
+	_panel = PanelContainer.new()
+	var style := UI.panel_style(ACCENT)
+	style.bg_color = Color(0.03, 0.06, 0.08, 0.93)
+	style.content_margin_left = 14
+	style.content_margin_right = 14
+	style.content_margin_top = 12
+	style.content_margin_bottom = 12
+	_panel.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", style)
+	_panel.position = Vector2(16, 140)
+	_panel.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(330, 0)
+	add_child(_panel)
+	var v := VBoxContainer.new()
+	v.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 6)
+	_panel.add_child(v)
+	v.add_child(UI.label(host.editor_title(), 18, ACCENT))
+	v.add_child(UI.section("TOOLS", ACCENT))
+	var group := ButtonGroup.new()
+	var grid := HFlowContainer.new()
+	grid.add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", 4)
+	grid.add_theme_constant_override("v_separation", 4)
+	v.add_child(grid)
+	for i in _tools.size():
+		var b := Button.new()
+		b.text = _tools[i]["label"]
+		var tid: String = _tools[i].get("id", "")
+		var how := ""
+		if _tools[i].get("rect", false):
+			how = "\nDrag a rectangle on the map."
+		elif _tools[i].get("drag", false):
+			how = "\nClick, or hold and drag to keep using it."
+		if _tools[i].has("options"):
+			how += "\nPick the kind in the list below the tools."
+		var more: String = {
+			"terrain": "Paints the ground kind chosen in the list (water and crevasses can't be walked on).\nThe brush size ([ / ]) sets how many tiles around the cursor are painted.",
+			"building": "Drag a rectangle (at least 3 x 3 tiles) to raise a Minoan building of the chosen style:\npalace, warehouse or temple. Its walls, doors, floors, roof and decor come from the tile sheets.",
+			"wall": "Each click cycles the wall under the cursor: plain, window, door. Doors are sliding doors\nthat open as people come near.",
+			"column": "Adds a Minoan column on a floor tile inside a building (columns block walking).",
+			"npc": "Places a Minoan citizen of the chosen kind where you click: a guard with a laser rifle, or an android\nwith a laser rifle, a laser bow or a labrys (the double axe). They stroll around that spot and shoot anything hostile.",
+			"prop": "Places scenery of the chosen kind (trees, palms, bushes, rocks, crystals...) - hold and drag to scatter it.",
+			"erase": "Removes what you click (citizens, scenery, columns, buildings) - hold and drag to erase as you go.\nStory ships in space can't be erased.",
+			"enemy": "Places a hostile ship of the chosen class where you click.",
+			"neutral": "Places a civilian ship (trader, miner, explorer) of the chosen class where you click.",
+			"asteroid": "Places an asteroid of the chosen ore where you click.",
+		}.get(tid, "")
+		how = ("\n" + more if more != "" else "") + how + "\nSave the layout (Ctrl+S) to keep your changes."
+		EditorIcons.dress(b, {"terrain": "terrain", "building": "building", "wall": "wall", "column": "column", "npc": "npc",
+			"prop": "prop", "erase": "erase", "enemy": "enemy", "neutral": "neutral", "asteroid": "asteroid"}.get(tid, "tool"),
+			EditorIcons.tip(_tools[i]["label"], str(i + 1) if i < 9 else "", str(_tools[i].get("help", "")) + how))
+		b.toggle_mode = true
+		b.button_group = group
+		b.alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT
+		b.focus_mode = FOCUS_NONE
+		b.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 15)
+		b.pressed.connect(_select_tool.bind(i))
+		grid.add_child(b)
+		_tool_buttons.append(b)
+	_options = OptionButton.new()
+	_options.focus_mode = FOCUS_NONE
+	_options.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 15)
+	_options.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Kind", "", "What the selected tool places or paints.")
+	_options.item_selected.connect(func(i): _opt = i)
+	v.add_child(_options)
+	_brush_row = HBoxContainer.new()
+	_brush_row.add_child(UI.label("Brush size", 14, UI.TEXT_DIM))
+	var slider := HSlider.new()
+	slider.min_value = 0
+	slider.max_value = 4
+	slider.step = 1
+	slider.value = _brush
+	slider.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(140, 24)
+	slider.size_flags_horizontal = SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	slider.focus_mode = FOCUS_NONE
+	var val := UI.label(str(_brush), 14)
+	slider.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Brush size", "[  /  ]", "How many tiles around the cursor the terrain brush paints (0 = one tile).")
+	slider.value_changed.connect(func(x): _brush = int(x); val.text = str(_brush))
+	_brush_slider = slider
+	_brush_row.add_child(slider)
+	_brush_row.add_child(val)
+	v.add_child(_brush_row)
+	v.add_child(UI.section("LAYOUT", ACCENT))
+	var lrow := HBoxContainer.new()
+	lrow.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)
+	v.add_child(lrow)
+	lrow.add_child(EditorIcons.dress(UI.button("Save layout", _save, 15), "save",
+		EditorIcons.tip("Save layout", "Ctrl+S", "Writes this map (terrain, buildings, citizens, scenery or ships) to its layout file in data/.\nIt's used every time from then on instead of the generated one.")))
+	lrow.add_child(EditorIcons.dress(UI.button("Revert to generated", func(): dirty = false; _status.text = host.editor_revert(), 15), "reload",
+		EditorIcons.tip("Revert to generated", "", "Deletes the saved layout: the map is generated again (as in a new game) next time it's loaded.")))
+	lrow.add_child(EditorIcons.docs_button(self, "level-editor"))
+	lrow.add_child(EditorIcons.dress(UI.button("Exit level editor", close, 15), "exit",
+		EditorIcons.tip("Exit the level editor", "F10 / Esc", "Back to the game (unsaved edits stay until you leave this map).")))
+	_status = UI.label("", 13, UI.TEXT_DIM)
+	_status.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
+	_status.custom_minimum_size.x = 300
+	v.add_child(_status)
+	v.add_child(UI.label("Left click: use tool  ·  1-9: pick tool  ·  Wheel: zoom\nWASD / arrows / middle-drag: pan  ·  [ ]: brush\nCtrl+S: save  ·  F1: docs  ·  F10 / Esc: exit  ·  Right-click: editor menu", 13, UI.TEXT_DIM))
+	UI.scale_fonts(_panel, "menu", 1.3)
+	PinTips.install(self, "level-editor")
+
+
+func _select_tool(i: int) -> void:
+	_tool = i
+	(_tool_buttons[i] as Button).set_pressed_no_signal(true)
+	var t: Dictionary = _tools[i]
+	_options.clear()
+	for o in t.get("options", []):
+		_options.add_item(str(o))
+	_options.visible = _options.item_count > 0
+	_opt = 0
+	if _options.visible:
+		_options.select(0)
+	_brush_row.visible = t.get("brush", false)
+	_status.text = t.get("help", "")
+
+
+func _save() -> void:
+	var path: String = host.editor_save()
+	dirty = path == "" and dirty
+	_status.text = ("Saved to " + path) if path != "" else "Save failed."
+	GameLog.post("[Dev] Layout saved", "info")
+
+
+func _world(screen: Vector2) -> Vector2:
+	return host.get_viewport().get_canvas_transform().affine_inverse() * screen
+
+
+func _apply(world: Vector2, phase: String) -> void:
+	dirty = true
+	var t: Dictionary = _tools[_tool]
+	var start: Vector2 = _drag_start if _drag_start != null else world
+	host.editor_apply(t["id"], _opt, _brush, world, phase, start)
+
+
+func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
+	if not visible or UI.esc_menu_open():
+		return
+	if event.is_action_pressed("ui_cancel"):
+		get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+		close()   # (Esc leaves the editor, as F10)
+		return
+	var k := event as InputEventKey
+	if k and k.pressed and not k.echo:
+		var done := true
+		if k.keycode >= KEY_1 and k.keycode <= KEY_9 and k.keycode - KEY_1 < _tools.size() and not k.ctrl_pressed:
+			_select_tool(k.keycode - KEY_1)
+		elif k.ctrl_pressed and k.keycode == KEY_S:
+			_save()
+		elif k.keycode == KEY_F10:
+			get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+			close()
+			return
+		elif k.keycode == KEY_F1:
+			EditorDocs.open(self, "level-editor", EditorDocs.FILE)
+		elif k.keycode in [KEY_BRACKETLEFT, KEY_BRACKETRIGHT] and _brush_slider:
+			_brush_slider.value += -1 if k.keycode == KEY_BRACKETLEFT else 1
+		else:
+			done = false
+		if done:
+			get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+			return
+	if not event is InputEventMouse:
+		return
+	if _panel.get_global_rect().has_point(event.position) and _drag_start == null and not _panning:
+		return  # the tool panel handles it
+	if event is InputEventMouseButton:
+		match event.button_index:
+			MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP, MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN:
+				if event.pressed:
+					var z := _cam.zoom.x * (1.12 if event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP else 1.0 / 1.12)
+					z = clampf(z, 0.25, 3.0)
+					_cam.zoom = Vector2(z, z)
+			MOUSE_BUTTON_MIDDLE:
+				_panning = event.pressed
+				if UI.middle_click(self, event):
+					_cam.zoom = Vector2.ONE   # (a middle click: the zoom back; a middle drag pans)
+			MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT:
+				if event.pressed:
+					UI.context_menu(self, event.position, [["Save layout  (Ctrl+S)", _save], ["Exit level editor  (F10)", close]])
+			MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT:
+				var w := _world(event.position)
+				if event.pressed:
+					_drag_start = w
+					_apply(w, "press")
+				elif _drag_start != null:
+					_apply(w, "release")
+					_drag_start = null
+	elif event is InputEventMouseMotion:
+		if _panning:
+			_cam.offset -= event.relative / _cam.zoom
+		elif _drag_start != null and _tools[_tool].get("drag", false):
+			_apply(_world(event.position), "drag")
+	get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	if not visible:
+		return
+	var d := Vector2.ZERO
+	if Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_A) or Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_LEFT): d.x -= 1
+	if Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_D) or Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_RIGHT): d.x += 1
+	if Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_W) or Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_UP): d.y -= 1
+	if Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_S) or Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_DOWN): d.y += 1
+	if d != Vector2.ZERO:
+		_cam.offset += d.normalized() * PAN_SPEED * delta / _cam.zoom.x
+	queue_redraw()
+
+
+## Tool cursor: brush circle or the rectangle being dragged.
+func _draw() -> void:
+	if _tools.is_empty():
+		return
+	var t: Dictionary = _tools[_tool]
+	var mouse := get_local_mouse_position()
+	var xf := host.get_viewport().get_canvas_transform()
+	if t.get("rect", false) and _drag_start != null:
+		var poly: PackedVector2Array = host.editor_rect_polygon(_drag_start, _world(mouse))
+		var pts := PackedVector2Array()
+		for p in poly:
+			pts.append(xf * p)
+		if pts.size() >= 3:
+			draw_colored_polygon(pts, Color(ACCENT, 0.18))
+			pts.append(pts[0])
+			draw_polyline(pts, ACCENT, 2.0, true)
+	elif t.get("brush", false):
+		var r := (40.0 + _brush * 90.0) * _cam.zoom.x
+		draw_arc(mouse, r, 0, TAU, 48, Color(ACCENT, 0.8), 2.0, true)
+	else:
+		draw_arc(mouse, 10.0, 0, TAU, 24, ACCENT, 2.0, true)
+		draw_line(mouse - Vector2(16, 0), mouse + Vector2(16, 0), Color(ACCENT, 0.6), 1.0)
+		draw_line(mouse - Vector2(0, 16), mouse + Vector2(0, 16), Color(ACCENT, 0.6), 1.0)

files.explanation: Talos, the game's editor: Versions - the Patcher (Talos > Versions, F7; the top of the rail): the game's patch notes, one entry per change - a short summary and a step-by-step infographic of what changed and how, drawn as vector graphics and animated step by step. Patches are data: data/patches/<id>.json {id, title, date, summary, steps: [{title, text, diagram: [element...]}]} Versions group patches: data/patches/version_<id>_<name>.json {kind: "version", id, title, date, summary, patches: [patch ids], steps: [{title, text, diagram, patch: <patch id>}]} - one page per patch The list is a tree: each version with its patches under it (newest first), patches in no version yet at the top level, unpublished changes first. Diagram elements live on a 1000 x 560 canvas (scaled to fit) - see PatchView for the kinds (box, text, arrow, circle, grid, iso, bar, badge, poly); each fades in after its "delay" (or one after another), "pulse" makes it glow. A patch can also carry a code review (the "Code review" tab): review: {intro, files: [{path, explanation, added, removed, hunks: [{title, note, diff (unified diff text), added, removed, bubbles: [{at, text}]}]}]} Bubbles explain how a part of the code works: each points (with an arrow) at the first diff line containing "at" (or line: its index in the diff), drawn over the code viewer in the empty space beside the code - see Bubbles. (Moved from scripts/patcher.gd.)

@@ -1,0 +1,1344 @@ 
+extends Control
+## Versions - the Patcher (Talos > Versions, F7; the top of the rail): the game's patch notes, one entry per
+## change - a short summary and a step-by-step infographic of what changed
+## and how, drawn as vector graphics and animated step by step.
+## Patches are data: data/patches/<id>.json
+##   {id, title, date, summary, steps: [{title, text, diagram: [element...]}]}
+## Versions group patches: data/patches/version_<id>_<name>.json
+##   {kind: "version", id, title, date, summary, patches: [patch ids],
+##    steps: [{title, text, diagram, patch: <patch id>}]}   - one page per patch
+## The list is a tree: each version with its patches under it (newest first),
+## patches in no version yet at the top level, unpublished changes first.
+## Diagram elements live on a 1000 x 560 canvas (scaled to fit) - see
+## PatchView for the kinds (box, text, arrow, circle, grid, iso, bar, badge,
+## poly); each fades in after its "delay" (or one after another), "pulse"
+## makes it glow.
+## A patch can also carry a code review (the "Code review" tab):
+##   review: {intro, files: [{path, explanation, added, removed,
+##            hunks: [{title, note, diff (unified diff text), added, removed,
+##                     bubbles: [{at, text}]}]}]}
+## Bubbles explain how a part of the code works: each points (with an arrow)
+## at the first diff line containing "at" (or line: its index in the diff),
+## drawn over the code viewer in the empty space beside the code - see Bubbles.
+
+const EDITOR_SCENE := "res://scenes/editor/editor.tscn"
+const DIR := "res://data/patches/"
+const ACCENT := Color(0.95, 0.7, 0.3)
+
+var patches: Array = []             # every entry, in the tree's order (a version, then its patches)
+## True while the unpublished changes are being scanned (a worker thread).
+var scanning := false
+var _task := -1
+var _parent: Array = []             # entry index -> its version's index (-1: top level)
+var _items: Array = []              # entry index -> its TreeItem
+var _selecting := false
+var current := -1
+var step := 0
+var _list: Tree
+var _title: Label
+var _date: Label
+var _summary: Label
+var _view: PatchView
+var _step_title: Label
+var _step_text: Label
+var _counter: Label
+var _open_patch: Button             # (a version's page: opens that page's patch)
+var _tabs: TabBar
+var _info_box: VBoxContainer        # the infographic
+var _review_box: VBoxContainer      # the code review
+var _review_intro: Label
+var _files: ItemList
+var _review: RichTextLabel
+var _bubbles: Bubbles               # (over the code viewer)
+var _mono: SystemFont
+var _asset_bar: HBoxContainer
+var _asset_info: Label
+var _player: AudioStreamPlayer
+var _rows: Array = []               # file list row -> index into the review's files (-1: all assets)
+var _tex_cache := {}
+const IMAGES := ["png", "jpg", "jpeg", "webp", "svg"]
+const SOUNDS := ["wav", "ogg", "mp3"]
+const FONTS := ["ttf", "otf"]
+const CODE := ["gd", "py", "gdshader", "glsl", "cs", "sh", "cpp", "h", "c"]   # (listed first in a review)
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	load_patches()
+	_build()
+	if not patches.is_empty():
+		show_patch(newest())
+
+
+## Where Versions opens: the newest version (or patch) - its infographic,
+## never the unpublished changes' code review.
+func newest() -> int:
+	for i in patches.size():
+		if not patches[i].get("pending", false):
+			return i
+	return 0
+
+
+## Reads every patch file (newest first).
+func load_patches() -> void:
+	patches = []
+	_parent = []
+	var found: Array = []
+	var versions: Array = []
+	var d := DirAccess.open(DIR)
+	if d != null:
+		for f in d.get_files():
+			if not f.ends_with(".json"):
+				continue
+			var p = _read(DIR + f)
+			if p is Dictionary and p.has("steps"):
+				p["file"] = f
+				if p.get("kind", "") == "version":
+					versions.append(p)
+				else:
+					found.append(p)
+	var newest := func(a, b): return str(a.get("date", "")) > str(b.get("date", "")) \
+		or (str(a.get("date", "")) == str(b.get("date", "")) and str(a.get("id", "")).naturalnocasecmp_to(str(b.get("id", ""))) > 0)
+	found.sort_custom(newest)
+	versions.sort_custom(newest)
+	# (the unpublished changes: scanned on a worker thread - a walk over the
+	# whole project, ~100 ms - and put at the top when ready: _add_pending)
+	if _task < 0:
+		scanning = true
+		_task = WorkerThreadPool.add_task(func(): _add_pending.call_deferred(unpublished()))
+	# Patches in no version yet: at the top, before the versions.
+	var grouped := {}
+	for v in versions:
+		for id in v.get("patches", []):
+			grouped[str(id)] = true
+	for p in found:
+		if not grouped.has(str(p.get("id", ""))):
+			patches.append(p)
+			_parent.append(-1)
+	for v in versions:
+		var vi := patches.size()
+		patches.append(v)
+		_parent.append(-1)
+		for p in found:
+			if str(p.get("id", "")) in v.get("patches", []).map(func(x): return str(x)):
+				patches.append(p)
+				_parent.append(vi)
+
+
+## Patch files, parsed, by path: [modified time, data] - 5 MB of JSON (the
+## code reviews) read again only when a file changes, not on every visit.
+static var _parsed := {}
+
+static func _read(path: String) -> Variant:
+	var t := FileAccess.get_modified_time(path)
+	if _parsed.has(path) and _parsed[path][0] == t:
+		return _parsed[path][1]
+	var p = JSON.parse_string(FileAccess.get_file_as_string(path))
+	_parsed[path] = [t, p]
+	return p
+
+
+## The unpublished changes, scanned (load_patches): joins the top of the list.
+func _add_pending(entry: Dictionary) -> void:
+	if _task >= 0:
+		WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion(_task)
+	_task = -1
+	scanning = false
+	if entry.is_empty() or not is_inside_tree():
+		return
+	if has_meta("talos_parked"):
+		_later = entry   # (Talos is on another tool: added when this one shows - talos_shown)
+		return
+	patches.insert(0, entry)
+	_parent = [-1] + _parent.map(func(x): return x if x < 0 else x + 1)
+	# Listed at the top; what you're looking at stays (the newest version's
+	# infographic, at first) - only its place in the list moves down one.
+	current += 1
+	_fill_list()
+	if current >= 0 and current < _items.size():
+		_selecting = true
+		_items[current].select(0)
+		_selecting = false
+
+
+var _later := {}
+
+## Talos shows the Patcher again: the unpublished changes found meanwhile.
+func talos_shown() -> void:
+	if not _later.is_empty():
+		var e := _later
+		_later = {}
+		_add_pending(e)
+
+
+func _exit_tree() -> void:
+	if _task >= 0:
+		WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion(_task)
+		_task = -1
+
+
+## What changed since the last published patch (from external/patcher/ - see
+## tools/patch.py; only when running from the project): an entry at the top
+## of the list with the change log and the changed files. {} if none / no tracking.
+const TRACK := "res://external/patcher/"
+const TRACKED := ["gd", "tscn", "tres", "gdshader", "json", "md", "cfg", "py", "godot", "txt", "svg",
+	"png", "jpg", "jpeg", "webp", "wav", "ogg", "mp3", "ttf", "otf"]
+
+func unpublished() -> Dictionary:
+	if not FileAccess.file_exists(TRACK + "manifest.json"):
+		return {}
+	var man = JSON.parse_string(FileAccess.get_file_as_string(TRACK + "manifest.json"))
+	if not man is Dictionary:
+		return {}
+	var known: Dictionary = man.get("files", {})
+	var times: Dictionary = man.get("mtimes", {})
+	var now := _tracked_files("res://")
+	var files := []
+	for p in now:
+		var kind := ""
+		if not known.has(p):
+			kind = "new"
+		elif int(times.get(p, 0)) != FileAccess.get_modified_time("res://" + p) and FileAccess.get_md5("res://" + p) != known[p]:
+			kind = "modified"
+		if kind != "":
+			files.append({"path": p, "kind": kind, "explanation": "%s since patch %s." % [kind.capitalize(), man.get("patch", "?")], "hunks": []})
+	var here := {}
+	for p in now:
+		here[p] = true
+	for p in known:
+		if not here.has(p):
+			files.append({"path": p, "kind": "deleted", "explanation": "Deleted since patch %s." % man.get("patch", "?"), "hunks": []})
+	var log := FileAccess.get_file_as_string(TRACK + "pending.md")
+	var titles := []
+	for l in log.split("\n"):
+		if l.begins_with("## "):
+			titles.append(l.substr(3))
+	if files.is_empty() and titles.is_empty():
+		return {}
+	return {"id": "pending", "pending": true, "title": "Unpublished changes", "date": "not yet a patch",
+		"summary": "%d change(s) logged since patch %s, %d file(s) changed: %s. Ask Claude to publish them as a patch entry when you're ready." % [
+			titles.size(), man.get("patch", "?"), files.size(), "; ".join(titles) if not titles.is_empty() else "(not logged yet)"],
+		"steps": [], "review": {"intro": log, "files": files}}
+
+
+func _tracked_files(dir: String) -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	var d := DirAccess.open(dir)
+	if d == null:
+		return out
+	for f in d.get_files():
+		if f.get_extension().to_lower() in TRACKED:
+			out.append((dir + f).trim_prefix("res://"))
+	for sub in d.get_directories():
+		if sub.begins_with(".") or sub in ["build", "export", "__pycache__"] or dir + sub + "/" == TRACK:
+			continue
+		out.append_array(_tracked_files(dir + sub + "/"))
+	return out
+
+
+func _build() -> void:
+	var root := TalosNav.wrap(UI.modal(self, ACCENT, Vector2.ZERO, true), "patcher", func(id): TalosNav.go(get_tree(), id))
+	var header: HBoxContainer = TalosNav.header("VERSIONS", "every version of the game and its patches: what changed, step by step", ACCENT)[0]
+	header.add_child(_btn("Replay", "reload", "R", "Plays this step's animation again.", func(): _view.restart()))
+	header.add_child(_btn("Reload patches", "open", "Ctrl+R", "Reads the patch files again (data/patches/).", func():
+		load_patches(); _fill_list(); show_patch(newest())))
+	header.add_child(EditorIcons.docs_button(self, "patcher"))
+	root.add_child(header)
+
+	var body := HBoxContainer.new()
+	body.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	body.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 12)
+	root.add_child(body)
+	_list = Tree.new()
+	_list.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(330, 0)
+	_list.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	_list.hide_root = true
+	_list.item_selected.connect(func():
+		var it := _list.get_selected()
+		if it and not _selecting:
+			show_patch(int(it.get_metadata(0))))
+	_list.tooltip_text = "Every version with its patches, newest first (Up / Down)."
+	body.add_child(_list)
+	_fill_list()
+
+	var right := VBoxContainer.new()
+	right.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	right.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 6)
+	body.add_child(right)
+	_title = UI.label("", 26, Color(1.0, 0.9, 0.7))
+	right.add_child(_title)
+	_date = UI.label("", 14, UI.TEXT_DIM)
+	right.add_child(_date)
+	# The summary: one paragraph.
+	var sp := PanelContainer.new()
+	var box := NeonTheme.box(Color(ACCENT, 0.5), Color(0.06, 0.05, 0.03, 0.85), 1, 6, 10)
+	box.content_margin_left = 14
+	box.content_margin_right = 14
+	sp.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", box)
+	_summary = UI.label("", 15, Color(0.92, 0.9, 0.85))
+	_summary.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
+	_summary.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(400, 0)
+	sp.add_child(_summary)
+	right.add_child(sp)
+	# Two views of the patch: the infographic and the code review.
+	_tabs = TabBar.new()
+	_tabs.add_tab("Infographic")
+	_tabs.add_tab("Code review")
+	_tabs.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	_tabs.tab_changed.connect(func(_t): _show_tab())
+	_tabs.tooltip_text = "Infographic: the change step by step (Tab switches).\nCode review: every changed file, as diffs with explanations."
+	right.add_child(_tabs)
+	_info_box = VBoxContainer.new()
+	_info_box.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	right.add_child(_info_box)
+	_review_box = VBoxContainer.new()
+	_review_box.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	_review_box.visible = false
+	right.add_child(_review_box)
+	_build_review()
+	# The infographic.
+	var nav := HBoxContainer.new()
+	nav.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 8)
+	nav.add_child(_btn("Previous step", "back", "Left", "The step before (on the first: the last).", func(): turn(-1)))
+	_counter = UI.label("", 15, ACCENT)
+	nav.add_child(_counter)
+	_step_title = UI.label("", 20, Color.WHITE)
+	_step_title.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	nav.add_child(_step_title)
+	_open_patch = _btn("Open this patch", "open", "Enter", "A version's page: opens the patch it's about.", open_page_patch)
+	nav.add_child(_open_patch)
+	nav.add_child(_btn("Next step", "forward", "Right / Space", "The next step (on the last: the first).", func(): turn(1)))
+	_info_box.add_child(nav)
+	_view = PatchView.new()
+	_view.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	_view.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(800, 420)
+	_view.clip_contents = true
+	_info_box.add_child(_view)
+	_step_text = UI.label("", 15, Color(0.85, 0.88, 0.95))
+	_step_text.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
+	_step_text.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(400, 0)
+	_info_box.add_child(_step_text)
+	UI.scale_fonts(root, "menu", 1.2)
+
+
+## The code review: the changed files (with how many lines were added and
+## removed) and, for the chosen file, what changed and why, hunk by hunk,
+## with the diff itself (+ added in green, - removed in red).
+func _build_review() -> void:
+	_review_intro = UI.label("", 14, UI.TEXT_DIM)
+	_review_intro.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
+	_review_intro.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(400, 0)
+	_review_box.add_child(_review_intro)
+	var split := HBoxContainer.new()
+	split.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	split.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 10)
+	_review_box.add_child(split)
+	# Playing a sound asset (shown for sounds only).
+	_asset_bar = HBoxContainer.new()
+	_asset_bar.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 8)
+	_asset_bar.visible = false
+	_asset_bar.add_child(_btn("Play the sound", "play", "", "Plays the sound asset (again to restart).", func():
+		if _player.stream: _player.play()))
+	_asset_bar.add_child(_btn("Stop", "stop", "", "Stops the sound.", func(): _player.stop()))
+	_asset_info = UI.label("", 14, UI.TEXT_DIM)
+	_asset_bar.add_child(_asset_info)
+	_review_box.add_child(_asset_bar)
+	_review_box.move_child(_asset_bar, 1)
+	_player = AudioStreamPlayer.new()
+	add_child(_player)
+	_files = ItemList.new()
+	_files.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(320, 0)
+	_files.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	_files.item_selected.connect(func(i): show_file(i))
+	_files.tooltip_text = "The files this patch changed: lines added / removed."
+	split.add_child(_files)
+	_mono = SystemFont.new()
+	_mono.font_names = PackedStringArray(["DejaVu Sans Mono", "Noto Sans Mono", "Liberation Mono", "Consolas", "Menlo", "Courier New", "monospace"])
+	_review = RichTextLabel.new()
+	_review.bbcode_enabled = true
+	_review.selection_enabled = true
+	_review.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	_review.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	_review.add_theme_font_override("mono_font", _mono)
+	_review.add_theme_font_size_override("mono_font_size", 13)
+	_review.add_theme_constant_override("line_separation", 4)   # (each diff line's background mustn't hide the underscores above)
+	_review.add_theme_font_size_override("normal_font_size", 15)
+	_review.add_theme_font_size_override("bold_font_size", 17)
+	var bg := StyleBoxFlat.new()
+	bg.bg_color = Color(0.03, 0.035, 0.06)
+	bg.set_content_margin_all(12)
+	_review.add_theme_stylebox_override("normal", bg)
+	split.add_child(_review)
+	_bubbles = Bubbles.new()
+	_bubbles.review = _review
+	_bubbles.font = _mono
+	_review.add_child(_bubbles)
+	_bubbles.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+
+
+func _show_tab() -> void:
+	_info_box.visible = _tabs.current_tab == 0
+	_review_box.visible = _tabs.current_tab == 1
+
+
+func _fill_review() -> void:
+	var rv: Dictionary = patches[current].get("review", {})
+	_tabs.set_tab_disabled(1, rv.is_empty())
+	if rv.is_empty() and _tabs.current_tab == 1:
+		_tabs.current_tab = 0
+	_review_intro.text = str(rv.get("intro", ""))
+	_files.clear()
+	_rows = []
+	var files: Array = rv.get("files", [])
+	var assets := 0
+	for f in files:
+		if _asset_kind(f["path"]) != "text":
+			assets += 1
+	# Code first, then the other text files, then the assets (each group in
+	# the review's order); the gallery of every asset heads the assets.
+	var order: Array = range(files.size())
+	order.sort_custom(func(a: int, b: int) -> bool:
+		var ga := _file_group(files[a]["path"])
+		var gb := _file_group(files[b]["path"])
+		return ga < gb or (ga == gb and a < b))
+	var gallery := assets > 1
+	for k in order:
+		var f: Dictionary = files[k]
+		if gallery and _file_group(f["path"]) == 2:   # a gallery of every asset
+			gallery = false
+			var g := _files.add_item("All assets  (%d)" % assets)
+			_files.set_item_custom_fg_color(g, Color(1.0, 0.8, 0.45))
+			_files.set_item_tooltip(g, "Every image, sound and font in this change, together.")
+			_rows.append(-1)
+		var kind := _asset_kind(f["path"])
+		var label := "%s   +%d  -%d" % [str(f["path"]).get_file(), int(f.get("added", 0)), int(f.get("removed", 0))]
+		if f.get("hunks", []).is_empty() and f.has("kind"):
+			label = "%s   (%s%s)" % [str(f["path"]).get_file(), f["kind"], "" if kind == "text" else ", " + kind]
+		var i := _files.add_item(label)
+		_files.set_item_tooltip(i, "%s\n%s" % [f["path"], f.get("explanation", "")])
+		_rows.append(k)
+	_review.clear()
+	_bubbles.clear()
+	_show_asset_bar(false)
+	if patches[current].get("pending", false):
+		# Unpublished changes: the change log in full (pick a file to see it).
+		_review_intro.text = "Changed since the last patch, not yet published - the change log, and the files (new, modified, deleted): pick one to see it. It becomes a patch entry when you ask Claude to publish it."
+		_review.append_text("[color=#dde3ee]%s[/color]" % _esc(str(rv.get("intro", ""))))
+	elif _files.item_count > 0:
+		show_file(0)
+
+
+## Where a file goes in the review's list: 0 code, 1 other text, 2 assets.
+func _file_group(path: String) -> int:
+	if _asset_kind(path) != "text":
+		return 2
+	return 0 if path.get_extension().to_lower() in CODE else 1
+
+
+## What a file is, for viewing: image, sound, font or text.
+func _asset_kind(path: String) -> String:
+	var e := path.get_extension().to_lower()
+	if e in IMAGES:
+		return "image"
+	if e in SOUNDS:
+		return "sound"
+	if e in FONTS:
+		return "font"
+	return "text"
+
+
+func _abs(path: String) -> String:
+	return ProjectSettings.globalize_path("res://" + path)
+
+
+## An image asset as a texture, read from the file itself (assets in external/
+## aren't imported), on a checkerboard so transparency shows. null if missing.
+func _image_texture(path: String, checker := true) -> Texture2D:
+	var key := "%s|%s" % [path, checker]
+	if _tex_cache.has(key):
+		return _tex_cache[key]
+	if not FileAccess.file_exists("res://" + path):
+		return null
+	var img := Image.new()
+	var err: int
+	if path.get_extension().to_lower() == "svg":
+		err = img.load_svg_from_string(FileAccess.get_file_as_string("res://" + path))
+	else:
+		err = img.load(_abs(path))
+	if err != OK or img.is_empty():
+		return null
+	img.convert(Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
+	if checker:
+		var bg := Image.create(img.get_width(), img.get_height(), false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
+		bg.fill(Color(0.2, 0.21, 0.25))
+		var c := 16
+		for y in range(0, img.get_height(), c):
+			for x in range(0, img.get_width(), c):
+				if (x / c + y / c) % 2 == 0:
+					bg.fill_rect(Rect2i(x, y, c, c), Color(0.27, 0.28, 0.33))
+		bg.blend_rect(img, Rect2i(Vector2i.ZERO, img.get_size()), Vector2i.ZERO)
+		img = bg
+	var tex := ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)
+	_tex_cache[key] = tex
+	return tex
+
+
+## A size that fits `box` (small images grow up to 2x, big ones shrink).
+func _fit(size: Vector2, box: Vector2) -> Vector2:
+	return size * minf(2.0, minf(box.x / size.x, box.y / size.y))
+
+
+func _show_asset_bar(on: bool, info := "") -> void:
+	_asset_bar.visible = on
+	_asset_info.text = info
+	if not on:
+		_player.stop()
+
+
+func _file_bytes(path: String) -> String:
+	var fa := FileAccess.open("res://" + path, FileAccess.READ)
+	if fa == null:
+		return "?"
+	var n := fa.get_length()
+	return "%.1f MB" % (n / 1048576.0) if n > 1048576 else "%d KB" % maxi(1, n / 1024)
+
+
+## Shows a list row: one changed file (its explanation, then the asset itself
+## or every hunk - title, note, diff), or the gallery of all assets.
+func show_file(row: int) -> void:
+	var files: Array = patches[current].get("review", {}).get("files", [])
+	if row < 0 or row >= _rows.size():
+		return
+	_files.select(row)
+	_review.clear()
+	_bubbles.clear()
+	_show_asset_bar(false)
+	var i: int = _rows[row]
+	if i < 0:
+		_show_gallery(files)
+		return
+	var f: Dictionary = files[i]
+	var b := "[font_size=20][color=#ffcf7a][b]%s[/b][/color][/font_size]   " % _esc(f["path"])
+	if f.get("hunks", []).is_empty() and _asset_kind(f["path"]) != "text":
+		b += "[color=#8a93a6]%s %s[/color]\n" % [f.get("kind", ""), _asset_kind(f["path"])]
+	else:
+		b += "[color=#6fd36f]+%d[/color]  [color=#ff6b5e]-%d[/color]\n" % [int(f.get("added", 0)), int(f.get("removed", 0))]
+	b += "[color=#dde3ee]%s[/color]\n\n" % _esc(str(f.get("explanation", "")))
+	if f.get("hunks", []).is_empty():
+		_review.append_text(b)
+		_show_asset(f)
+		_review.scroll_to_line(0)
+		return
+	var n := 1
+	var code: Dictionary = {}   # paragraph -> the code line shown in it (the others: full-width text)
+	var points: Array = []      # [paragraph, bubble text]
+	for h in f.get("hunks", []):
+		b += "[color=#7fd8ff][b]%d.  %s[/b][/color]   [color=#8a93a6]+%d -%d[/color]\n" % [n, _esc(h["title"]), int(h.get("added", 0)), int(h.get("removed", 0))]
+		b += "[color=#cfd6e4]%s[/color]\n" % _esc(str(h.get("note", "")))
+		b += "[code]"
+		var diff := str(h["diff"]).split("\n")
+		var first := b.count("\n")
+		for k in diff.size():
+			code[first + k] = diff[k].replace("\t", "    ")
+		for bu in h.get("bubbles", []):
+			var at := bubble_line(diff, bu)
+			if at >= 0:
+				points.append([first + at, str(bu.get("text", ""))])
+		for l in diff:
+			var line := _esc(l.replace("\t", "    "))
+			match l.left(1):
+				"+":
+					b += "[bgcolor=#0f3a1c][color=#9df5a6]%s[/color][/bgcolor]\n" % line
+				"-":
+					b += "[bgcolor=#45161a][color=#ffaaa2]%s[/color][/bgcolor]\n" % line
+				"@":
+					b += "[color=#8ab4ff]%s[/color]\n" % line
+				_:
+					b += "[color=#7d8596]%s[/color]\n" % line
+		b += "[/code]\n"
+		n += 1
+	_review.append_text(b)
+	_review.scroll_to_line(0)
+	_bubbles.show_points(code, points)
+
+
+## The diff line a bubble points at: the first containing its "at" (added
+## lines first), or its "line" (an index in the diff); -1: none.
+static func bubble_line(diff: PackedStringArray, bubble: Dictionary) -> int:
+	if bubble.has("line"):
+		var k := int(bubble["line"])
+		return k if k >= 0 and k < diff.size() else -1
+	var at := str(bubble.get("at", ""))
+	if at.is_empty():
+		return -1
+	for pass_ in 2:
+		for k in diff.size():
+			if (pass_ == 1 or diff[k].begins_with("+")) and not diff[k].begins_with("@@") and diff[k].contains(at):
+				return k
+	return -1
+
+
+## The asset of a file without a diff: the picture, a sound to play, a font
+## sample, or the text itself.
+func _show_asset(f: Dictionary) -> void:
+	var path: String = f["path"]
+	if f.get("kind", "") == "deleted":
+		_review.append_text("[color=#ff9a8a](deleted - no longer in the project)[/color]\n")
+		return
+	if not FileAccess.file_exists("res://" + path):
+		_review.append_text("[color=#ff9a8a](no longer in the project - it was moved or deleted since)[/color]\n")
+		return
+	match _asset_kind(path):
+		"image":
+			var tex := _image_texture(path)
+			if tex == null:
+				_review.append_text("[color=#ff9a8a](couldn't read the image)[/color]\n")
+				return
+			_review.append_text("[color=#8a93a6]%d x %d px  ·  %s[/color]\n" % [tex.get_width(), tex.get_height(), _file_bytes(path)])
+			var sz := _fit(Vector2(tex.get_size()), Vector2(maxf(200.0, _review.size.x - 40.0), 520.0))
+			_review.add_image(tex, int(sz.x), int(sz.y))
+			_review.add_text("\n")
+		"sound":
+			var stream := _load_sound(path)
+			_player.stream = stream
+			var info := "%s  ·  %s" % [path.get_file(), _file_bytes(path)]
+			if stream:
+				info += "  ·  %.1f s" % stream.get_length()
+			_show_asset_bar(stream != null, info)
+			_review.append_text("[color=#cfd6e4]A sound: play it with the button above.[/color]\n" if stream else "[color=#ff9a8a](couldn't read the sound)[/color]\n")
+		"font":
+			var font := FontFile.new()
+			if font.load_dynamic_font(_abs(path)) != OK:
+				_review.append_text("[color=#ff9a8a](couldn't read the font)[/color]\n")
+				return
+			for fs in [14, 22, 34]:
+				_review.push_font(font, fs)
+				_review.add_text("Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow - 0123456789\n")
+				_review.pop()
+		_:
+			var text := FileAccess.get_file_as_string("res://" + path)
+			var lines := text.split("\n")
+			var shown := "\n".join(lines.slice(0, 400))
+			_review.append_text("[code][color=#cfd6e4]%s[/color][/code]" % _esc(shown.replace("\t", "    ")))
+			if lines.size() > 400:
+				_review.append_text("\n[color=#8a93a6](... %d more lines)[/color]" % (lines.size() - 400))
+
+
+func _load_sound(path: String) -> AudioStream:
+	match path.get_extension().to_lower():
+		"ogg":
+			return AudioStreamOggVorbis.load_from_file(_abs(path))
+		"mp3":
+			var m := AudioStreamMP3.new()
+			m.data = FileAccess.get_file_as_bytes("res://" + path)
+			return m
+		"wav":
+			return AudioStreamWAV.load_from_file(_abs(path))
+	return null
+
+
+## Every asset of the change together: pictures as thumbnails with their
+## names; sounds and fonts listed (pick one to play / see it).
+func _show_gallery(files: Array) -> void:
+	_review.append_text("[font_size=20][color=#ffcf7a][b]All assets[/b][/color][/font_size]\n[color=#8a93a6]Pick one in the list to see it full size (or to play a sound).[/color]\n\n")
+	var cols := maxi(2, int((_review.size.x - 40.0) / 190.0))
+	_review.push_table(cols)
+	var others := []
+	for f in files:
+		if _asset_kind(f["path"]) != "image":
+			if _asset_kind(f["path"]) != "text":
+				others.append(f)
+			continue
+		_review.push_cell()
+		var tex := _image_texture(f["path"])
+		if tex:
+			var sz := _fit(Vector2(tex.get_size()), Vector2(170, 170))
+			_review.add_image(tex, int(sz.x), int(sz.y))
+		else:
+			_review.append_text("[color=#ff9a8a](missing)[/color]")
+		_review.append_text("\n[font_size=12][color=#cfd6e4]%s[/color][/font_size]\n " % _esc(str(f["path"]).get_file()))
+		_review.pop()
+	_review.pop()
+	for f in others:
+		_review.append_text("\n[color=#cfd6e4]%s  (%s)[/color]" % [_esc(f["path"]), _asset_kind(f["path"])])
+
+
+func _esc(s: String) -> String:
+	return s.replace("[", "[lb]")
+
+
+func is_version(i: int) -> bool:
+	return i >= 0 and i < patches.size() and patches[i].get("kind", "") == "version"
+
+
+func _fill_list() -> void:
+	_list.clear()
+	_items = []
+	var root := _list.create_item()
+	for i in patches.size():
+		var p: Dictionary = patches[i]
+		var parent: TreeItem = root if _parent[i] < 0 else _items[_parent[i]]
+		var it := _list.create_item(parent)
+		if p.get("pending", false):
+			it.set_text(0, "●  %s" % p["title"])
+			it.set_custom_color(0, Color(1.0, 0.75, 0.35))
+		elif is_version(i):
+			it.set_text(0, "Version %s  ·  %s" % [p.get("id", "?"), p.get("title", "")])
+			it.set_custom_color(0, Color(1.0, 0.86, 0.5))
+		else:
+			it.set_text(0, "%s  ·  %s" % [p.get("id", ""), p.get("title", p.get("id", "?"))])
+		it.set_metadata(0, i)
+		it.set_tooltip_text(0, "%s\n%s" % [p.get("title", ""), p.get("summary", "")])
+		_items.append(it)
+
+
+func show_patch(i: int) -> void:
+	if i < 0 or i >= patches.size():
+		return
+	current = i
+	if i < _items.size():
+		_selecting = true
+		_items[i].select(0)
+		_list.scroll_to_item(_items[i])
+		_selecting = false
+	var p: Dictionary = patches[i]
+	_title.text = ("Version %s  ·  %s" % [p.get("id", ""), p.get("title", "")]) if is_version(i) else str(p.get("title", ""))
+	if p.get("pending", false):
+		_date.text = "not published yet  ·  tools/patch.py status for the details"
+	elif is_version(i):
+		_date.text = "%s  ·  version %s  ·  %d patches  ·  a page for each" % [p.get("date", ""), p.get("id", ""), p.get("patches", []).size()]
+	else:
+		var v := "" if _parent[i] < 0 else "  ·  in version %s" % patches[_parent[i]].get("id", "")
+		_date.text = "%s  ·  patch %s  ·  %d steps%s" % [p.get("date", ""), p.get("id", ""), p["steps"].size(), v]
+	_summary.text = str(p.get("summary", ""))
+	_fill_review()
+	_tabs.set_tab_disabled(0, p["steps"].is_empty())
+	if p["steps"].is_empty():
+		_tabs.current_tab = 1   # (unpublished changes: no infographic yet)
+	else:
+		_tabs.current_tab = 0   # (an entry always opens on its infographic, not the code)
+	_show_tab()
+	go_step(0, true)
+
+
+## Shows step i (clamped to the steps there are). Past the last step (or
+## before the first) nothing happens - the step stays as it is, its diagram
+## isn't replayed; force: show it anyway (a newly opened entry).
+func go_step(i: int, force := false) -> void:
+	if current < 0:
+		return
+	var steps: Array = patches[current]["steps"]
+	if not force and not steps.is_empty() and clampi(i, 0, steps.size() - 1) == step:
+		return
+	if steps.is_empty():
+		_open_patch.visible = false
+		_counter.text = ""
+		_step_title.text = ""
+		_step_text.text = ""
+		_view.show_diagram([])
+		return
+	step = clampi(i, 0, steps.size() - 1)
+	var s: Dictionary = steps[step]
+	if is_version(current):
+		_counter.text = "Page %d / %d%s" % [step + 1, steps.size(), ("  ·  patch %s" % s["patch"]) if s.has("patch") else ""]
+	else:
+		_counter.text = "Step %d / %d" % [step + 1, steps.size()]
+	_open_patch.visible = is_version(current) and _page_patch() >= 0
+	_step_title.text = str(s.get("title", ""))
+	_step_text.text = str(s.get("text", ""))
+	_view.show_diagram(s.get("diagram", []))
+
+
+## Next (by 1) / Previous (by -1) step, going round: Next on the last step
+## shows the first, Previous on the first the last.
+func turn(by: int) -> void:
+	if current >= 0 and not patches[current]["steps"].is_empty():
+		go_step(posmod(step + by, patches[current]["steps"].size()))
+
+
+## The entry of the patch the version's current page is about (-1: none).
+func _page_patch() -> int:
+	if not is_version(current):
+		return -1
+	var s: Dictionary = patches[current]["steps"][step]
+	for k in patches.size():
+		if not is_version(k) and not patches[k].get("pending", false) and str(patches[k].get("id", "")) == str(s.get("patch", "")):
+			return k
+	return -1
+
+
+func open_page_patch() -> void:
+	var k := _page_patch()
+	if k >= 0:
+		show_patch(k)
+
+
+func _back() -> void:
+	TalosNav.go(get_tree(), "menu")   # (Esc: as the rail's Exit)
+
+
+func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
+	if not (event is InputEventKey and event.pressed and not event.echo):
+		return
+	var k := event as InputEventKey
+	match k.keycode:
+		KEY_RIGHT, KEY_SPACE:
+			turn(1)
+		KEY_LEFT:
+			turn(-1)
+		KEY_DOWN:
+			show_patch(current + 1)
+		KEY_UP:
+			show_patch(current - 1)
+		KEY_R:
+			if k.ctrl_pressed:
+				load_patches(); _fill_list(); show_patch(newest())
+			else:
+				_view.restart()
+		KEY_ENTER, KEY_KP_ENTER:
+			open_page_patch()
+		KEY_TAB:
+			_tabs.current_tab = 1 - _tabs.current_tab if not _tabs.is_tab_disabled(1) else 0
+		KEY_ESCAPE:
+			get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()   # (before: leaving frees the scene)
+			_back()
+			return
+		KEY_F1:
+			EditorDocs.open(self, "patcher", EditorDocs.FILE)
+		_:
+			return
+	get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+
+
+func _btn(name: String, icon: String, keys: String, help: String, cb: Callable) -> Button:
+	var b := UI.button("", cb, 14)
+	b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	return EditorIcons.dress(b, icon, EditorIcons.tip(name, keys, help))
+
+
+## Draws one step's diagram: vector elements on a 1000 x 560 canvas scaled
+## to fit, each fading / sliding in (arrows draw themselves, bars fill),
+## pulsing ones glowing. Elements ({"t": kind, ...}, positions in canvas px;
+## colours "#rrggbb" or a name from COLORS):
+##   box     rect [x,y,w,h], fill, stroke, label, size, color, r (corner)
+##   text    at [x,y], text (\n for lines), size, color, align left/center/right
+##   arrow   from, to, color, width, label, bend (sideways bow, px), dashed
+##   circle  at, r, fill, stroke, label
+##   grid    rect, cols, rows, fill, stroke, cells [[col,row,colour]...]
+##   iso     at (centre), w (width; height w / 2), n (grid lines), fill, stroke,
+##           marks [[u,v,colour,size,label]...], areas [[u,v,du,dv,colour,dashed]...] (0..1)
+##   bar     rect, value 0..1, color, label, track
+##   badge   at (centre), text, color, size
+##   poly    points [[x,y]...], fill, stroke, closed
+## Any element: delay (s), pulse (true).
+class PatchView extends Control:
+	const W := 1000.0
+	const H := 560.0
+	## The smallest text in a diagram (its units): shown at 86% at 1920 x 1080
+	## (the Versions page), that's 14 px - never under Settings.MIN_FONT.
+	const MIN_TEXT := 16
+	const COLORS := {"cyan": Color(0.35, 0.85, 1.0), "gold": Color(1.0, 0.78, 0.3), "green": Color(0.45, 0.9, 0.45),
+		"red": Color(0.95, 0.35, 0.3), "blue": Color(0.35, 0.55, 1.0), "purple": Color(0.7, 0.5, 1.0),
+		"white": Color(0.95, 0.95, 0.97), "dim": Color(0.55, 0.6, 0.7), "dark": Color(0.08, 0.1, 0.16),
+		"panel": Color(0.11, 0.14, 0.22), "land": Color(0.3, 0.55, 0.3), "forest": Color(0.18, 0.42, 0.25),
+		"sea": Color(0.15, 0.35, 0.6), "sand": Color(0.85, 0.75, 0.5), "stone": Color(0.85, 0.72, 0.55)}
+	var elements: Array = []
+	var t := 0.0
+	var _font: Font
+
+	func _ready() -> void:
+		_font = ThemeDB.fallback_font
+
+	func show_diagram(els: Array) -> void:
+		elements = els
+		restart()
+
+	func restart() -> void:
+		t = 0.0
+		queue_redraw()
+
+	func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+		t += delta
+		queue_redraw()
+
+	func _col(v: Variant, fallback: Color) -> Color:
+		if v == null:
+			return fallback
+		if v is Color:
+			return v
+		var s := str(v)
+		if COLORS.has(s):
+			return COLORS[s]
+		return Color.from_string(s, fallback)
+
+	func _p(v: Variant) -> Vector2:
+		return Vector2(float(v[0]), float(v[1]))
+
+	func _draw() -> void:
+		draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size), Color(0.035, 0.045, 0.08))
+		# A faint blueprint grid behind everything.
+		var k := minf(size.x / W, size.y / H)
+		var off := (size - Vector2(W, H) * k) / 2.0
+		draw_set_transform(off, 0.0, Vector2(k, k))
+		for x in range(0, int(W) + 1, 40):
+			draw_line(Vector2(x, 0), Vector2(x, H), Color(0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 0.06), 1.0)
+		for y in range(0, int(H) + 1, 40):
+			draw_line(Vector2(0, y), Vector2(W, y), Color(0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 0.06), 1.0)
+		for i in elements.size():
+			var e: Dictionary = elements[i]
+			var delay := float(e.get("delay", 0.15 + i * 0.12))
+			var a := clampf((t - delay) / 0.4, 0.0, 1.0)
+			if a <= 0.0:
+				continue
+			var ease := 1.0 - pow(1.0 - a, 3.0)
+			var glow := 0.0
+			if e.get("pulse", false):
+				glow = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin((t - delay) * 4.0)
+			draw_set_transform(off + Vector2(0, (1.0 - ease) * 14.0 * k), 0.0, Vector2(k, k))
+			_element(e, ease, glow)
+		draw_set_transform(Vector2.ZERO)
+
+	func _element(e: Dictionary, a: float, glow: float) -> void:
+		match str(e.get("t", "")):
+			"box":
+				var r := Rect2(_p(e["rect"]), Vector2(float(e["rect"][2]), float(e["rect"][3])))
+				var sb := StyleBoxFlat.new()
+				sb.bg_color = Color(_col(e.get("fill"), COLORS["panel"]), _col(e.get("fill"), COLORS["panel"]).a * a)
+				var st := _col(e.get("stroke"), COLORS["cyan"])
+				sb.border_color = Color(st.lightened(0.3 * glow), a)
+				sb.set_border_width_all(int(e.get("border", 2)) + (1 if glow > 0.5 else 0))
+				sb.set_corner_radius_all(int(e.get("r", 10)))
+				sb.anti_aliasing = true
+				if glow > 0.0:
+					sb.shadow_color = Color(st, 0.35 * glow * a)
+					sb.shadow_size = 12

+	## An element's text size (its `size`, else `default`), never under MIN_TEXT.
+	static func text_size(e: Dictionary, default: int) -> int:
+		return maxi(MIN_TEXT, int(e.get("size", default)))
+
+	## Where an arrow's label goes: above the middle of its curve.
+	static func arrow_label_at(e: Dictionary) -> Vector2:
+		var f := Vector2(float(e["from"][0]), float(e["from"][1]))
+		var to := Vector2(float(e["to"][0]), float(e["to"][1]))
+		var mid := (f + to) / 2.0 + (to - f).orthogonal().normalized() * float(e.get("bend", 0.0))
+		return (f.lerp(mid, 0.5)).lerp(mid.lerp(to, 0.5), 0.5) + Vector2(0, -12)
+
+	## The rectangles a line-by-line text covers (as _lines draws it).
+	static func _line_rects(font: Font, s: String, at: Vector2, fs: int, align: String) -> Array:
+		var out := []
+		var y := at.y
+		for l in s.split("\n"):
+			var w := font.get_string_size(l, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs).x
+			var x := at.x - (w / 2.0 if align == "center" else (w if align == "right" else 0.0))
+			if w > 2.0:   # (an empty line covers nothing)
+				out.append(Rect2(x, y - font.get_ascent(fs), w, font.get_ascent(fs) + font.get_descent(fs)))
+			y += fs * 1.25
+		return out
+
+	## What's wrong with a diagram's text, at the sizes it's drawn (MIN_TEXT
+	## and up): a label wider or taller than its box, text off the canvas,
+	## two elements' texts over each other. [] - all readable.
+	static func lint(els: Array, font: Font) -> Array:
+		var out := []
+		var texts := []   # [element index, rect]
+		for i in els.size():
+			var e: Dictionary = els[i]
+			var tag := "%d %s" % [i, str(e.get("t", ""))]
+			match str(e.get("t", "")):
+				"box":
+					if str(e.get("label", "")) == "":
+						continue   # (a frame round other things)
+					var r := Rect2(float(e["rect"][0]), float(e["rect"][1]), float(e["rect"][2]), float(e["rect"][3]))
+					var fs := text_size(e, 18)
+					var lines := str(e["label"]).split("\n")
+					for l in lines:
+						if font.get_string_size(l, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs).x > r.size.x - 12.0:
+							out.append("%s: \"%s\" wider than its box (%d)" % [tag, l, r.size.x])
+					if lines.size() * fs * 1.25 > r.size.y - 4.0:
+						out.append("%s: %d lines taller than its box (%d)" % [tag, lines.size(), r.size.y])
+					# (its lines, as _text_in places them - a box can frame other things)
+					var lh := fs * 1.25
+					var y := r.get_center().y - lh * lines.size() / 2.0 + fs * 0.95
+					for l in lines:
+						var w := font.get_string_size(l, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs).x
+						if w > 2.0:
+							texts.append([i, Rect2(r.get_center().x - w / 2.0, y - font.get_ascent(fs), w, font.get_ascent(fs) + font.get_descent(fs))])
+						y += lh
+					continue
+				"text":
+					for r in _line_rects(font, str(e["text"]), Vector2(float(e["at"][0]), float(e["at"][1])), text_size(e, 18), str(e.get("align", "left"))):
+						texts.append([i, r])
+				"arrow":
+					if e.has("label"):
+						for r in _line_rects(font, str(e["label"]), arrow_label_at(e), text_size(e, 15), "center"):
+							texts.append([i, r])
+				"circle":
+					if e.has("label"):
+						var at := Vector2(float(e["at"][0]), float(e["at"][1])) + Vector2(0, float(e.get("r", 10)) + 16)
+						for r in _line_rects(font, str(e["label"]), at, text_size(e, 14), "center"):
+							texts.append([i, r])
+				"bar":
+					if e.has("label"):
+						var at := Vector2(float(e["rect"][0]) + 14, float(e["rect"][1]) + float(e["rect"][3]) / 2.0 + 6)

+							texts.append([i, r])

+					var p := Vector2(float(e["at"][0]), float(e["at"][1]))
+					var tw := font.get_string_size(str(e["text"]), HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs).x

+	func _dash(a: Vector2, b: Vector2, c: Color, w: float) -> void:
+		var n := maxi(2, int(a.distance_to(b) / 10.0))
+		for i in range(0, n, 2):
+			draw_line(a.lerp(b, float(i) / n), a.lerp(b, float(i + 1) / n), c, w, true)
+
+	## Text centred in a rectangle (several lines).
+	func _text_in(s: String, r: Rect2, fs: int, c: Color) -> void:
+		var lines := s.split("\n")
+		var lh := fs * 1.25
+		var y := r.get_center().y - lh * lines.size() / 2.0 + fs * 0.95
+		for l in lines:
+			draw_string(_font, Vector2(r.position.x, y), l, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER, r.size.x, fs, c)
+			y += lh
+
+	func _lines(s: String, at: Vector2, fs: int, c: Color, align: String, outline := false) -> void:
+		var y := at.y
+		for l in s.split("\n"):
+			var w := _font.get_string_size(l, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs).x
+			var x := at.x
+			if align == "center":
+				x -= w / 2.0
+			elif align == "right":
+				x -= w
+			if outline:   # (readable over any fill)
+				draw_string_outline(_font, Vector2(x, y), l, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs, 5, Color(0, 0, 0, 0.7 * c.a))
+			draw_string(_font, Vector2(x, y), l, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs, c)
+			y += fs * 1.25
